cites.title: Lumber Pioneer Gone: Late Adam Pershbaker's Fortune Amassed On Coquille, The Sunday Oregonian (Portland, Oregon), 4 March 1917, p. 49
cites.repository: GenealogyBank
cites.quote: John Pershbaker built the first sawmill on Coos Bay In 1867, while Adam Pershbaker, in 1887, erected at Prosper the nucleus of the plant which has grown into one of the largest mills on the Coquille River. Adam Pershbaker was born in St. Charles County, Missouri, July 1; 1838. Following the Civil War, through which he served for three years, he came West, settling in California in 1866. Practically penniless, he came to Coos County in 1870 to undertake his first business venture, a general merchandise store, at the old town of Randolph, seven miles up the river from Bandon.
cites.translation: John Pershbaker built the first sawmill on Coos Bay in 1867, while Adam Pershbaker, in 1887, erected at Prosper the nucleus of the plant which has grown into one of the largest mills on the Coquille River. Adam Pershbaker was born in St. Charles County, Missouri, July 1, 1838. Following the Civil War, through which he served for three years, he came West, settling in California in 1866. Practically penniless, he came to Coos County in 1870 to undertake his first business venture, a general merchandise store, at the old town of Randolph, seven miles up the river from Bandon.
cites.note: Born 1 July 1838 in St. Charles County, Missouri; served three years in the Union Army during the Civil War; came West to California in 1866 and settled in Coos County, Oregon in 1870/1871 (where his brother John Pershbaker had built the first sawmill on Coos Bay in 1867); opened the first general merchandise store in the Coquille Valley at Randolph (seven miles up the Coquille River from Bandon), owned the Black Sand gold mines and townsite of Randolph in the 1870s, and in 1887/1888 erected at Prosper one of the largest sawmills on the Coquille River.
cites.why: Biographical tribute in The Sunday Oregonian (4 March 1917, p. 49) and obituary in The Morning Oregonian (19 February 1917, p. 4) naming his daughters Mrs. S. W. Fahy of Prosper and Mrs. Andrew Muir of Oakland, CA.

His es- i tate of $250,000 is left to two daughters, Mrs. S. W. Fdhy, of Prosper, and Mrs, Andrew Muir, of Oakland, Cal. The funeral will.be held here Tuesday.
cites.translation: COOS EARLY SETTLER DEAD / Adam Pershbaker Stricken Suddenly at Age of 79. BANDON, Or., Feb. 18.—(Special.)—Adam Pershbaker, prominent early settler of Coos County, died suddenly at Prosper last night at the age of 79 years. He came to the county in 1871, was the first merchant in the Coquille Valley, owned the famous Black Sand mines and townsite of Randolph during the gold rush in the '70s and built the Prosper sawmill in 1888. His estate of $250,000 is left to two daughters, Mrs. S. W. Fahy, of Prosper, and Mrs. Andrew Muir, of Oakland, Cal. The funeral will be held here Tuesday.
cites.note: Died suddenly Saturday night, 17 February 1917, at Prosper, Coos County, Oregon, age 78 (reported as 79); funeral held at Bandon, Oregon on Tuesday, 20 February 1917; left an estate estimated at $250,000–$850,000 to his two daughters, Mrs. S. W. Fahy of Prosper, Oregon, and Mrs. Andrew Muir of Oakland, California.
cites.why: Published death dispatches from Bandon in The Morning Oregonian (19 February 1917, pp. 4, 15) and the Oregon Journal (19 February 1917, p. 8) naming his two surviving daughters Mrs. S. W. Fahy of Prosper and Mrs. Andrew Muir of Oakland, CA.

cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. ‖ 10. | 58. | dessen Frau Anne | 38. / dessen Frau Anne | 21. / Tochter Anne | 5.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now. His wife Anne, 38; [Jahn's] wife Anne, 21; daughter Anne, 5.
cites.note: 1857 soul revision, family 10/58, XIX Gibboi farm: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth' (Jahn's son Mārcis, the farmer, head of the farm), 34½ at the last revision (1850), now 41½ (b. c. 1816); 'dessen Frau Anne', 38 (b. c. 1819). With them: his brothers 2. Jahn (35; wife Anne 21; son Marz b. 1855) and 3. Dahw (25½ in 1850, gone by 1857), and 'Tochter Anne', 5 (b. c. 1852), entered after Jahn's wife, so the page leaves open whether she is Mārcis's daughter or Jahn's. No Marija: Marija Gibboja (b. 1853) is 'Marri, 4' in the Rauguļi household of the other Marz Gibboi, 50 (image 16).
cites.why: Read at full size, both pages (Round 3). Mārcis, Jahn's son, 41½, is the Mārcis Ģibols b. 1816, son of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847), of Raimonds's tree: age and father agree. His wife Anne, 38, is the Anna b. 1819 whom the tree calls Anna Balodis (the surname is the tree's alone).
cites.as_recorded: Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth; dessen Frau Anne

cites.title: Pēteris Sirlaks
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 10.08.1847 Miršanas datums: 10.11.1896 … Tēva vārds: Mārcis … Kapsēta: Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi … Marija Sirlaka — Sieva — 00.00.1853 – 00.00.1925
cites.translation: Born 10 Aug 1847, died 10 Nov 1896; father's name Mārcis; cemetery Jaunrauna (Priekuļi parish); wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925
cites.note: Timenote gives Pēteris Sirlaks 10 Aug 1847 – 10 Nov 1896, son of Mārcis and Anna Sirlaks, buried in Jaunrauna cemetery (Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi). Wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925, NOT 1920 as in the 2015 tree. Children: Natalie 1875–1887, Ernestīne 1879, Mārtiņš 1884–1942, Dāvis 1886–1952, Kristīne 1888, Anna 1890 (the memoir's aunt Anna in Rīga), Augusts 1895. 1938 court notices (Valdības Vēstnesis) mention mortgages issued by a Pēteris Sirlaks, with inheritance shares under a 16 Apr 1915 division act going to Augusts, Ernestīne and Anna Sirlaks. Very likely the same family's farm, which would place the estate division in 1915. PROBABLE SOURCE OF THE 2015 DATES: MyHeritage 'Jurcins Web Site' by Māris Jurciņš (Latvia), whose public name index spells her 'Marija Sirlaka (Ģībojs)', 'Marija Gilboy' and 'Gibboja (Ģībojs)'. 'Gibboja' is exactly the 2015 tree's spelling. Peter emailed himself 'Sirlaks myheritage.com genealogy' on 2018-11-16. MyHeritage pages are behind an hCaptcha and were NOT opened. Marija's maiden name 'Ģībojs/Gibboja' should be verified in the Jaunrauna/Rauna church books.
cites.why: Timenote's exact dates match the 2015 tree for Pēteris; the MyHeritage spelling 'Gibboja' matches. Both are user trees without a cited record, so they are derivative until checked against the Rauna/Jaunrauna registers (Raduraksti).

cites.title: Rauna births 1889 no. 243
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, img 432 (right page)
cites.quote: September, dritten, morgens 2 U. | achten. | 243. Ronneburg, Lappul. Anna Smukkul. Elt. Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch. Pth. Mch. Karline Kahjon, Jg. Jahn Kahjon, W. Mari Meesiht. Get. v. Pastor Dsirne in der Kirche.
cites.translation: Born 3 September, 2 a.m.; baptised 8th. No. 243. Rauna, Lapuļi. Anna Smukkul. Parents: farmhand Dāvis Smukkul and wife Mari née Kahjon, both Lutheran. Godparents: maiden Karlīne Kahjon, bachelor Jānis Kahjon, wife Mari Meesiht. Baptised by Pastor Dsirne in the church.
cites.note: Born 3 Sep 1889 at 2 a.m. (Julian; 15 Sep 1889 Gregorian), baptised 8 Sep 1889 by Pastor Dsirne in the church. Legitimate daughter of 'Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch' (farmhand Dāvis Smukulis and wife Marija née Kajons, married 28 Oct 1884 in Rauna, 1884 no. 42). Godparents: 'Mch. Karline Kahjon, Jg. Jahn Kahjon, W. Mari Meesiht'. Younger full biological sister of Emma Smukkul (b. 25 Dec 1885 Jul. = 6 Jan 1886 Greg. at Lubar, Lj: Luhzmann, 1886 no. 33, to the same parents 'Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Marie geb. Kahjon', with Meesiht godparents 'Md. Juhle Meesiht' and 'Jg. August Meesiht'); by Sep 1889 the family had moved from Lubāra (Lūcmaņi) to Rauna manor's Lapuļi farm (where Wth. Peter Kahjon × Anna geb. Mise also lived in 1886–1890). Crucially, at the baptism of Emma Smukule and Mārtiņš Vilhelms Sirlaks's daughter Elvīra Antonija Sirlaka on 19 Feb 1912 (Rīga St Martin 1912 no. 82), the godmother from the mother's side was 'Anna Smukul' — Emma's younger full sister Anna (b. Sep 1889, age 22 in Feb 1912).
cites.why: Parents' names and mother's maiden name ('Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon') are identical to 1884 marriage no. 42 and Emma Smukkul's 1886 birth no. 33, both sisters share Meesiht godparents, and Anna is the exact match for the 1912 godmother Anna Smukul.

notes: Emma Smukule's younger full sister, born at Lapuļi farm, Rauna (1889 no. 243); godmother to her niece Elvīra in Rīga, 1912.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 58 | — | 68 / XIV Meschzeem | Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn | 30 | — | 40 / Marz des Jahns 1te Sohn | 6 | — | 16 / Jahn ,, 2te Sohn | 2½ | — | 12½ ‖ XIV Meschzeem | Masche deßen Weib | 50 / XIV Meschzeem | Liese deßen Weib | 40 / Mareet ihre 1te Tochter | 14½ / Anne ihre 2te Tochter | 4
cites.translation: Surname XIV Meschzeem: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 58 -> 68; his wife Masche, 50. Jahn, Jacob's 1st son, 30 -> 40; his wife Liese, 40; Jahn's 1st son Marz, 6 -> 16; 2nd son Jahn, 2½ -> 12½; their 1st daughter Mareet, 14½; their 2nd daughter Anne, 4.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 1826 surname revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 54, ff. 49v–50r), farm 1. Meschzeem, surname No. XIV Meschzeem (second farmer's household): farmer Jacob, Jahn's son ('Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, now 68 (b. c. 1758), and his wife Masche, age 50 (b. c. 1776); Jacob's 1st son Jahn ('Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn'), age 30 in 1816, now 40 (b. c. 1786), and his wife Liese, age 40 (b. c. 1786); their sons 1. Marz (6 -> 16) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 12½); their daughters 1. Mareet (14½) and 2. Anne ('Anne ihre 2te Tochter'), age 4 in 1826 (born c. 1822). Also listed are Jacob's 2nd son Dawe (16 in 1816, 's. in No 10'), 4th son Jacob (2½ -> 12½), daughters Juhle (17) and Masche (15), and farmer's brother Peter, Jahn's son ('Peter, Jahns Sohn Wirthsbruder', 47 -> 57; wife Anne, 41).
cites.why: Identifies Anne Meschzeem at age 4 in the 1826 surname revision with her parents Jānis Mežciems (40) × Līze (40), paternal grandparents Jēkabs Jāņa d. Mežciems (68) × Maža (50), and paternal great-grandfather Jānis (Jahn).
cites.as_recorded: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth; Masche deßen Weib; Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn; Liese deßen Weib; Anne ihre 2te Tochter

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1834, I. Meschzeem, family 1
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1. | Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth | 58 | 1832 gestorben | — / dessen Sohn 1 Jahn | 29 | 1833 gestorben | — / dessen Söhne 1 Marz | 6 | — | 24 / 2 Jahn | 2½ | — | 20½ / 2 Dawe | 16 | vide N XXVIII | — / 3 Jakob jetziger Wirth | 2½ | — | 20½ ‖ 1 | dessen Wittwe Masche | 57 / dessen Wittwe Lihse | 47 / dessen Frau Babbe | 22 / dessen Töchter 1 Mareet | 21½ / 2 Anne | 11
cites.translation: Family 1: Jakob Meschzeem, former farmer, 58 [in 1816], died in 1832; his widow Masche, 57. His 1st son Jahn, 29 [in 1816], died in 1833; his widow Lihse, 47. His [Jahn's] sons: 1. Marz, 6 -> 24 (his wife Babbe, 22); 2. Jahn, 2½ -> 20½; his [Jahn's] daughters: 1. Mareet, 21½; 2. Anne, 11. [Jakob Sr.'s sons:] 2. Dawe, 16, see No. XXVIII; 3. Jakob, current farmer, 2½ -> 20½.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 117, ff. 115v–116r), farm I. Meschzeem, family no. 1: former farmer Jakob Meschzeem ('Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, died in 1832 ('1832 gestorben'), leaving widow Masche, age 57; his 1st son Jahn ('dessen Sohn 1 Jahn'), age 29 in 1816, died in 1833 ('1833 gestorben'), leaving widow Lihse, age 47; Jahn's sons 1. Marz (6 -> 24; wife Babbe, 22) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 20½); Jahn's daughters 1. Mareet (21½) and 2. Anne (11, born c. 1822/23). Jakob's 3rd son Jakob (2½ -> 20½) is now the current farmer ('3 Jakob jetziger Wirth').
cites.why: Records the exact death years of Anne Meschzeem's grandfather Jēkabs Mežciems (died 1832) and father Jānis Mežciems (died 1833), and shows 11-year-old Anne Meschzeem with her widowed mother Līze (47) and grandmother Maža (57) at I. Meschzeem.
cites.as_recorded: 1. Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth (1832 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Masche; dessen Sohn 1 Jahn (1833 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Lihse; dessen Töchter 1 Mareet, 2 Anne

cites.title: Declaration of Intention No. 134, Arvids Danenbergs, Mercer County Common Pleas, Celina, Ohio, 14 Aug 1950

cites.quote: (5) I was born on Jan. 17, 1913 in Sturumuiza Latvia
cites.note: Gregorian date. The FamilySearch tree (LR39-9HZ) and the SSDI have 4 Jan 1913, which is the same day in the Julian (Old Style) calendar still used in Russian Courland in 1913 (a 13-day difference). The NUMIDENT, the Michigan death index, the declaration of intention and both obituaries all have 17 Jan. "Sturumuiza" is probably a manor/farm (muiža) name. Auce is the nearest town. cites.title: Talsi agronomy bureau (1942–1944)
cites.repository: National Library of Latvia (periodika.lv) & Elvīra Danenberga memoir
cites.locator: Daugavas Vanagu Mēnešraksts, Nr.2 (01.04.1996), section beginning p. 46
cites.quote: Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, dzimis 1913.g. 17. janvārī Tukuma apriņķa Stūrmuižas pagastā. Pēc 2.Jelgavas valsts ģimnāzijas beigšanas studē Lauksaimniecības Akadēmijā Jelgavā, ko beidz ar agronoma grādu. Strādā Talsu agronomiskā birojā. 1941.g. no Sv. Jāņa baznīcas Cēsīs uzsāk kopīgu ģimenes dzīvi ar farmaceiti Elvīru Širlaku. 1944.g. Arvīds ar sievu, 2 gadus vecu dēlu Pēteri un sievas māti Emmu Širlaku dodas bēgļu gaitās uz Vāciju. Tur turpina izglītību Štutgartes—Hohenheimas agrikultūras augstkolā, kur iegūst mākstera grādu agronomijā. 1949.g. izceļo uz ASV. … Miris pēkšņā nāvē auto katastrofā 1996. g. 19. februārī, atstājot sievu Elvīru, trīs bērnus — Pēteri, Kalvi, Līgu, 3 mazbērnus ASV, brāli Žani un vairākus radus Latvijā. Pārpelnots un pelnu urna nosūtīta uz Latviju.
cites.translation: Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, born 17 January 1913 in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district. After finishing the 2nd Jelgava State Gymnasium he studied at the Agricultural Academy in Jelgava, graduating as an agronomist. He worked at the Talsi agronomy bureau. In 1941, from St John's church in Cēsis, he began family life with the pharmacist Elvīra Širlaka [sic]. In 1944 Arvīds, his wife, their two-year-old son Pēteris and his wife's mother Emma Širlaka fled as refugees to Germany. There he continued his studies at the Stuttgart-Hohenheim agricultural college, earning a master's degree in agronomy. In 1949 he emigrated to the USA. … Died suddenly in a car accident on 19 February 1996, survived by his wife Elvīra, three children (Pēteris, Kalvis, Līga), 3 grandchildren in the USA, his brother Žanis and several relatives in Latvia. Cremated; the urn was sent to Latvia.
cites.note: 17 January is the New Style date; 4 January 1913 (Old Style) = 17 January 1913 (New Style), which reconciles the FamilySearch date 1913-01-04. Middle name Fricis. The 1983 jubilee note instead says "Vecauces pag." (Vecauce parish, Jelgava district), and the Laiks and Latvija Amerikā obituaries say "Tukumā", so the place is uncertain between Stūrmuiža (Tukums district) and Vecauce.
cites.why: Three independent exile-press notices give 17 Jan 1913; the parish differs between them (Stūrmuiža / Tukums / Vecauce). Identity is certain (wife Elvīra, children Pēteris, Kalvis, Līga).

cites.translation: MAKING IT HOME LIKE—Arvids Danenbergs, Latvian displaced person who was brought to Mercer County, O., under the sponsorship of St. Paul's Lutheran Church in Mercer County, starts trimming the lawn at the tenant home on the D. R. Smalley farm, where he and his wife, three children, Peter, Liga and Kalvis, shown above, will reside. ... The Danenbergs lived in Talsi, Latvia, until 1944, when the German troops took over their farm and forced them westward into Germany. After the fall of Berlin they were placed in an American DP camp. Mr. Danenbergs's parents, who remained at Talsi, later were sent to Siberia by the Russians. The eight Latvians came to the United States from Bremerhaven aboard the U.S. Army Transport Gen. Blatchford.
cites.note: Residing in the tenant house on the D. R. Smalley farm in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio, working under farm manager Carl Hawk under the sponsorship of St. Paul's Lutheran Church in Liberty Township (Rev. Grant Shealey, pastor), accompanied by wife Elvira (37), children Peter (6) and twins Liga and Kalvis (2 1/2), and mother-in-law Mrs. Emma Sirlaks, after arriving from Bremerhaven aboard the U.S. Army Transport Gen. Blatchford and previously living in Talsi, Latvia until 1944 (where he held an agricultural position similar to an American county agent; the article also reports that his parents remained at Talsi and were later sent to Siberia by the Russians) and in an American DP camp in Germany.
cites.why: Contemporary 13 July 1949 dispatch and photographs of Arvīds and Elvīra Danenbergs, their children Peter, Liga, and Kalvis, and mother-in-law Emma Sirlaks at the tenant house on the D. R. Smalley farm in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio.

cites.title: Household of Arwids F Danenbergs, Liberty Township, Mercer, Ohio
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: 136 No No Danenbergs, Arwids F Head W M 37 Mar Latvia … WK … 70 Farm Hand Farm P
cites.note: 1950 census, ED 54-34, sheet 16, lines 14-22, dwelling 136, enumerator Bernice Fetters. Head, 37, farm hand, born Latvia. Household: Elvira A (wife, 38), Peter V (son, 7, b. Latvia), Liga (daughter, 3, b. Germany), Kalvis V (son, 3, b. Germany), Emma Sirlaks (mother-in-law, 65, widowed, b. Latvia), Witolds Balks (brother-in-law, 29, farm hand), Biruta Z Balks (sister-in-law, 30), Ilze Balks (niece, 4, b. Germany). Line 30 on the same sheet, the next dwelling but three, is HAWK, Robert M., 25, farmer: very likely the "Hawk farm" sponsor in the memoir. So the first US home was in Mercer County (Rockford/Celina), not Seneca County (Tiffin). Tiffin comes later. In April 1950 Mirdza addressed her mother "c/o E. Sirlaks - D. R. Smalley Farms, Rockford, Ohio" (see the Detroit card below).
cites.why: Every name, age and relationship matches the memoir and the declarations.

cites.title: Obituary of Arvids F. Danenbergs (unnamed Cass County paper)
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: Mr. Arvids F. Danenbergs, 83, 56882 Point Rd., Kelsey Lake, Cassopolis, died Monday, Feb. 19, 1996 at Lee Memorial Hospital in Dowagiac, after injuries received in a two car accident in Penn Township. He was born Jan. 17, 1913 in Auce, Latvia.

She survives with a daughter, Liga Schubach of Milwaukee; two sons, Peter Danenberg'of Altadena, Calif., and Kalvis Danenbergs of Midland, Ohio;- three grandchildren; and a brother, Zanis of Latvia, He was a member of the Local Latvian Community Gar- ezers, Three Rivers, and studied agriculture and science.

cites.title: Augusts Sirlaks in interwar Latvia and at his sister Anna's funeral in Rīga
cites.repository: Aina Jurciņa (née Sirlaka) memoir
cites.quote: Redzāju Augustu divas reizi. Viņš neradojās. Esot komunists. Reiz vasarā “Vīstuču” pagalmā viņš stāvēja, rokā laikraksts “Cīņa”. Tas bija Latvijas laikā. Otreiz laikam Rīgas tantas bērēs, Stabu ielā pie bēru vakariņām. Viņam blakus sēdēja viņa draudzene.
cites.note: Returned to Latvia after the 1922 prisoner exchange; his niece Aina Jurciņa recalled seeing him twice in Latvia — once in summer at Vīstuči during the interwar republic holding the newspaper Cīņa, and a second time at the funeral supper of his sister Anna ('Rīgas tante', d. 29 December 1963) on Stabu iela in Rīga in December 1963 / January 1964.

cites.quote: He is survived by his children, Dennis Greashaber of Blue Springs, Mo., Daryl Greashaber of Marion, Allyson (Terry) Haycox of Marion, Derrick (Anna) Greashaber of Marion, Linda (John) Sabo of North Ridgeville, Oh., Doug (Sonya) Greashaber of Marion, Dean (Lorri) Greashaber of Marion, Barbara (Justin) Danenbergs of Columbus, Oh., 14 grandchildren and 8 great grandchildren.

cites.title: DANE GREASHABER Obituary (1928–2018) — Marion, OH
cites.repository: Legacy.com / Ann Arbor News (MLive)
cites.quote: GREASHABER, DANE ALDEN age 90 of Marion, Ohio formerly of Milan, Michigan passed away Monday, April 2, 2018. He was born February 23, 1928 in Milan, Mi., to the late Walter and Pearl (Goldsmith) Greashaber. On April 24, 1948 he married Irma Ann (Burger) Greashaber, she preceded him in death on August 3, 2002.
cites.note: Her parents were DANE ALDEN GREASHABER (b. 23 February 1928 at Milan, Michigan; d. Monday 2 April 2018 at Marion, Ohio, aged 90; son of Walter and Pearl (Goldsmith) Greashaber) and IRMA ANN (BURGER) GREASHABER (married him 24 April 1948; died 3 August 2002). Dane worked for Kroger in Michigan for 21 years, then moved the family to Marion, Ohio, where he owned Dane's Fairpark Foodland for 11 years, and afterwards worked three years at Archway Cookies. In retirement he played euchre at the Marion and Pleasant Senior Centers, bowled, pitched horseshoes and followed Michigan football and basketball and the Detroit Tigers. Funeral at Marion Bible Fellowship, 5 April 2018, Deacon Kevin Kehn officiating; burial Grand Prairie Cemetery, Marion. His brothers Robert and Harold and sisters Frances Bliss and Margaret Ann Blain predeceased him. Barbara is the youngest of eight children: Dennis (Blue Springs, Missouri), Daryl (Marion), Allyson (Terry) Haycox (Marion), Derrick (Anna) (Marion), Linda (John) Sabo (North Ridgeville, Ohio), Doug (Sonya) (Marion), Dean (Lorri) (Marion), and Barbara. 14 grandchildren and 8 great-grandchildren in 2018.
cites.why: Her father's own published obituary, which names her as his daughter with her husband and city.

facts.place: Mariposa, Mariposa County, California, United States
facts.value: Inducted with the first Mariposa contingent: he left Mariposa on Wednesday 19 Sep 1917 for training at Camp Lewis (Pierce Co., WA), home of the 91st Division. This independently corroborates the VA master index card (FamilySearch Q5GN-L53Z): '316 MP / 91st Div'.

Private, drafted 22 Sep 1917 at Mariposa, California. Assigned on original draft arrival at Camp Lewis (4 Oct 1917) to Company 12, 166th Depot Brigade, and transferred on 23 Oct 1917 to Company "A", 316th Military Police, 91st Division, per Special Orders No. 55, Headquarters 91st Division,…

Promoted to Private, 1st Class between 31 Dec 1917 and 28 Feb 1918, and assigned Army serial number 2274478 when serial numbers were first issued in February 1918 (Company "A", 316th Military Police assigned the consecutive block 2274450+ in strict alphabetical order across its Privates 1st Class:…

cites.translation: KILLED BY AN ENGINE / Rev. C. Alderson Meets Death on Track at Albany. ALBANY, Or., Oct. 12.—Rev. C. Alderson, a retired pioneer Methodist minister, whose home was at Salem, was instantly killed this morning by the engine of a freight train. He was hurled from a trestle 30 feet down and forward to the rocks of Pennywinkle Creek, this city. His skull was crushed by the fall. ... The Rev. Christopher Alderson was born in Yorkshire, England, September 11, 1827, and came to the United States in 1850. He crossed the plains in 1852, and settled in Oregon. He was married to Mary C. Royal, August 13, 1862, and she survives him. ... He is survived by his widow, Mrs. Mary C. Alderson, two sons, Professor W. C. Alderson, of St. Johns, and W. S. Alderson, of Portland; four daughters, Mrs. Margaret Burkhart, of Albany, and Mrs. Anna Pearson, of Ashland, Or.; Miss Edith R. and Miss Lola Alderson, residing with their mother in Salem. The funeral services will be held in the Sunnyside Methodist Episcopal Church, East Yamhill and Thirty-fifth streets, Monday afternoon at 2 o'clock.
cites.note: Retired pioneer Methodist minister whose home was in Salem, Oregon; instantly killed on the morning of Saturday, 12 October 1907 at Albany, Linn County, Oregon, when struck by a freight train engine on the middle trestle while walking on the track to the depot after visiting his daughter (Mrs. Margaret Burkhart) in Albany, falling 30 feet to the rocks of Pennywinkle Creek; born 11 September 1827 in Yorkshire, England, immigrated to the United States in 1850, crossed the plains to Oregon in 1852, entered the Oregon Conference ministry in 1856, and married Mary C. Royal on 13 August 1862; survived by widow Mrs. Mary C. Alderson, sons Prof. W. C. Alderson of St. Johns and W. S. Alderson of Portland, and daughters Mrs. Margaret Burkhart of Albany, Mrs. Anna Pearson of Ashland, and Miss Edith R. and Miss Lola Alderson of Salem; funeral Monday, 14 October 1907 at Sunnyside Methodist Episcopal Church (E. Yamhill and 35th Sts., Portland).
cites.why: Detailed news obituary in The Sunday Oregonian (13 October 1907, p. 28) matching birth date (11 Sep 1827), death date and place (12 Oct 1907, Albany, OR), spouse Mary C. Royal, and children including W. S. Alderson of Portland.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.
cites.as_recorded: Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi, 2. Jahn, 3. Dahw

cites.title: Rauna Latvian congregation births and baptisms 1877–1891, 1886 no. 134
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, image 322 (right page, folio 314)
cites.quote: April, vierten, nachmittags 3 U. | April dreizehnten | 134 Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz. Dawid Sirlak. Elt. Wth Peter Sirlak u. d. Fr. Marie geb. Gibboy, beide lutherisch. Pth. Wth Dahw Bitte, Wth Mahrz Sirnis u. d. Fr. Lihse. Get. vom Wirth Dahw Gudre im Hause, bestät. den 10 August v. Past. [Sirne?] in d. K.
cites.translation: Born 4 April, 3 p.m.; baptised 13 April. No. 134. Neuhof, Lower Vīstuči: Dawid Sirlak. Parents: farmer Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte; farmer Mahrz Sirnis and his wife Lihse. Baptised at home by farmer Dahw Gudre; confirmed 10 August by Pastor [Sirne?] in church.
cites.note: Born 4 Apr 1886 Julian (= 16 Apr 1886 Gregorian), 3 p.m.; baptised at home 13 Apr 1886 by farmer Dahw Gudre, confirmed (bestätigt) in church 10 Aug 1886 by the pastor [Sirne?]. Legitimate son of farmer (Wirth) Peter Sirlak and his wife Marie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: farmer Dahw Bitte; farmer Mahrz Sirnis and his wife Lihse. Same parents and farm as Mārtiņš Vilhelms (1883 no. 324), so the two are full brothers. The relative's tree date 4 Apr 1886 is the Julian date.
cites.why: Name, date (exactly the tree's 4 Apr 1886), farm, father and mother (with the 'Gibboy' spelling) all match; Dāvis Sirlaks, farm owner, is godfather of Mārtiņš's daughter Elvīra in 1912.

cites.title: Aina Jurciņa
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Obituary: Edith Evelyn Leslie (Dec. 21, 1916 – Feb. 8, 2018), The World (Coos Bay, Oregon), 17 February 2018
cites.repository: GenealogyBank
cites.quote: Dec. 21, 1916 – Feb. 8, 2018 At Edith's request, there will be no service for Edith Evelyn Leslie, 101, formerly of Bandon. She died Feb. 8, 2018 at home in Eugene. The descendant of pioneers in Coos County, Edith loved spending most of her retirement living on the family ranch near Bandon. She was born Dec. 21, 1916, in Oakland, Calif., to Andrew Robertson Muir and Ruby Edith (Pershbaker) Muir. An only child, she was raised in the countryside near Los Gatos where her favorite playmates were her beloved dogs, cats, ducks and geese. After graduating from a preparatory school for young ladies, Edith became one of the first women to enter Stanford University, where she studied art. She earned a liberal arts degree from the University of Washington in 1937 and her teacher's credential from the University of California at Berkeley in 1938. She married Williamar Leslie, a fellow Stanford student from Mountain View, Calif., June 2, 1941, in the Stanford Memorial Chapel. They made their first home in Wilmington, Dela., and Williamar commuted to his job as a market analyst on Wall Street until a position with U.S. Steel in San Francisco, Calif., brought them back to the West Coast. Edith and Williamar lived in Berkeley, Calif., where Edith taught English to recent immigrants. They raised three children, Lael, Lorin, and Lann, in a home filled with parrots, iguanas, geese, geckos, lizards and Edith's art work. When Williamar retired in 1969, they decided to build a house on the Coquille River ranch that Edith's grandfather Adam Pershbaker, a mill owner and the founder of Prosper, had purchased shortly before she was born.
cites.note: Died Thursday, 8 February 2018 at home in Eugene, Oregon (living with her son Lann Leslie and his wife Melody), age 101, from complications of head injuries sustained in an accidental fall in late January; born 21 December 1916 in Oakland, California, only child of Andrew Robertson Muir and Ruby Edith (Pershbaker) Muir; raised near Los Gatos, studied art at Stanford University, earned a B.A. from the University of Washington in 1937 and a teaching credential from UC Berkeley in 1938; married Williamar Leslie on 2 June 1941 at Stanford Memorial Chapel; lived in Wilmington, Delaware, and Berkeley, California (raising children Lael, Lorin, and Lann) before retiring in 1969 to the Coquille River ranch near Bandon purchased by her grandfather Adam Pershbaker; received the National Wetlands Conservation Award from the U.S. Department of Fish and Wildlife in 1995.
cites.why: Full published obituary in The World (Coos Bay, Oregon), 17 February 2018, naming parents Andrew Robertson Muir and Ruby Edith (Pershbaker) Muir, grandfather Adam Pershbaker, husband Williamar Leslie (d. 1992), and children Lael, Lorin, and Lann (wife Melody).

cites.title: Biographical notes on Paul Fitz Gibbon, Elaine de la Balt, Monya, and John Grattan Fitz Gibbon Sr.
cites.repository: Peter Danenberg, 2015 Genealogical Database
cites.quote: Elaine eventually became a nurse, moved to East Bay, and there met Paul Fitz Gibbon. … eventually resided with Elaine and Paul Fitz Gibbon in Berkeley, along with her last husband (a retired Russian sea-captain).
cites.note: After emigrating from Russia and becoming a nurse, she moved to the East Bay in California, married neurosurgeon Paul Fitz Gibbon (with whom she had son John Grattan Fitz Gibbon Sr. on 1934), and resided with him and her mother Monya in Berkeley, Alameda County, California.
cites.why: The span 1932/1934 bounds their move to the East Bay / Berkeley between the end of Paul Fitz Gibbon's Green Bay Packers football career ('from 1930-2') and the 1934 birth of their son John Grattan Fitz Gibbon Sr.

cites.title: Mūsu jubilāri
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Elvīrai Danenbergai, dzim. Sirlaka, piepildījās 75 mūža gadi. Dzimusi 1912. g. 9. janv. Rīgā. Skolas gadus pavadījusi Cēsīs. 1941. g. beigusi LU Ķīmijas fakultātes Farmācijas nod. ar maģistra grādu. Strādājusi Rīgā un vairākās provinces aptiekās. ASV apmetusies Ohio, un kopā ar vīru agr. Arvīdu uzaudzināja 2 dēlus un meitu. Strādāja par farmaceiti Tiffin Ohio. Pārceļoties uz Mičigenu, dzīvo savā farmā Garezera tuvumā.
cites.translation: Elvīra Danenberga, née Sirlaka, turned 75. Born 9 Jan 1912 in Rīga. Spent her school years in Cēsis. In 1941 graduated from the Pharmacy Section of the Chemistry Faculty of the University of Latvia with a master's degree. Worked in Rīga and several provincial pharmacies. In the USA settled in Ohio and with her husband, the agronomist Arvīds, raised 2 sons and a daughter. Worked as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. Moving to Michigan, she lives on her farm near Garezers.
cites.note: Schooling in Cēsis. In 1941 she graduated from the Pharmacy Section of the Chemistry Faculty of the University of Latvia with a master's degree ("maģistra grāds"). She worked in Rīga and several provincial pharmacies, and in the USA as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. 9 January is confirmed by DV Milwaukee birthday lists for 2002, 2003 and 2006.
cites.why: 75th-birthday note names her maiden name and husband Arvīds; it matches the memoir (Rīga 1912, Cēsis, pharmacy). The day is repeated in three later notices.

cites.title: Rīga St Martin Latvian congregation 1912, births and baptisms no. 82
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 68, image 15 (right page, bottom)
cites.quote: 1911 Декабря двадцать седьмого (27) 7 ч. веч. | 1912 Февраля девятнадцатаго (19) | № 82 | Эльвира Антонія (Elvira Antonie). Род. торговецъ Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Сирлакъ (Sirlak) ев. лют. вѣр. и его жена Эмма, ур. Смукулъ ев. лют. вѣроиспов. Воспр.: Давидъ Сирлакъ, хозяинъ; Анна Смукулъ, дѣв.; Эрнестина Сирлакъ, дѣвица. Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]
cites.translation: Born 27 December 1911, 7 p.m.; baptised 19 February 1912. No. 82. Elvira Antonie. Parents: trader Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Lutheran, and his wife Emma née Smukul, Ev.-Lutheran. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. Baptised [in …] by Pastor Hilde[?].
cites.note: Born 27 Dec 1911 Julian (= 9 Jan 1912 Gregorian) at 7 p.m.; baptised 19 Feb 1912 Julian (= 3 Mar 1912 Gregorian). Full baptismal name Elvira Antonie. Father: trader (торговецъ) Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Luth.; mother: his wife Emma née Smukul (the ending '-улъ' written over a struck-out ending), Ev.-Luth. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner (хозяинъ) [= her uncle Dāvis]; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. The last line, in another hand, reads roughly 'Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]' — baptised [at …] by Pastor Hilde[?]; place uncertain. Entry no. 82 sits among March baptisms, i.e. it was registered late, which is why date-ordered searches missed it. No residence is given (so Torņakalns is not confirmed here).
cites.why: Birth date to the hour matches the memoir's 9 Jan 1912 (= 27 Dec 1911 Julian); father's double name Martin Wilhelm and mother Emma née Smukul match; godparents are a Sirlaks farm owner David (her uncle Dāvis of Vīstuči) and a Smukul.

cites.repository: GenealogyBank
cites.quote: Crash victim moved to nursing home DOWAGIAC — Elvira Dan- enbergs, 84, of 56882 Point Road, Cassopolis, has been moved from Bronson Methodist Hospital, Kalamazoo, to a nursing home, according to a hospital spokesman. Danenbergs had been treated in the hospital’s trauma care unit since a two-car crash Feb. 19 that claimed the life of her husband, Arvids Danenbergs, 83. The acci; dent occurred about 2:45 p.m. at; the intersection of Decatur Road and Dutch Settlement Street.
cites.translation: Crash victim moved to nursing home DOWAGIAC — Elvira Danenbergs, 84, of 56882 Point Road, Cassopolis, has been moved from Bronson Methodist Hospital, Kalamazoo, to a nursing home, according to a hospital spokesman. Danenbergs had been treated in the hospital's trauma care unit since a two-car crash Feb. 19 that claimed the life of her husband, Arvids Danenbergs, 83. The accident occurred about 2:45 p.m. at the intersection of Decatur Road and Dutch Settlement Street.
cites.note: Residing at 56882 Point Road, Cassopolis, Michigan; injured on 19 February 1996 in the two-car crash at Decatur Road and Dutch Settlement Street (six miles east of Dowagiac) that killed her husband Arvids Danenbergs; freed from the wreckage by Cassopolis Fire Department rescue squad, treated in the trauma care unit at Bronson Methodist Hospital, Kalamazoo, upgraded from serious to fair on 24 February 1996, and transferred to a nursing home by 1 March 1996.
cites.why: Named with exact street address (56882 Point Road, Cassopolis), age (84), and husband Arvids Danenbergs (83) across three South Bend Tribune reports (20 Feb, 24 Feb, and 1 Mar 1996).

cites.quote: Emīlis savu dzimtas koku iestādīja 15 gadus vēlāk nekā Davids- 1930.gadā. … Emīlis savu sievu lūkot brauca gulbeniešos- Bēniņu dzimtā. Tajā 5 meitas: Alma, Elza, Olga, Zelma, Mildiņa un dēls Jānis. … Uz “Vīstučiem” atveda Elzu ar garām zeltainām bizēm.

cites.title: Elza Sirlaka at Kalna Vīstuči (1930–1949, 1956–1988)
cites.repository: Aina Jurciņa memoir & Raimonds Voroņins MyHeritage tree
cites.quote: Uz “Vīstučiem” atveda Elzu ar garām zeltainām bizēm. … | Emīlis Sirlaks | "Kalna Vīstučos" | … Viņa sieva Elza- pati labsirdība- vienmēr mums šuva kleitas

cites.title: Declaration of Intention No. 132, Mrs. Emma Sirlaks
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: Mrs. Emma Sirlaks … Housewife … 65 … Jan. 6, 1885 in Branti, Latvia … I am widowed … Elvira Danenbergs-F- Jan. [overwritten] 1912--Riga, Latvia--Rockford, Ohio / Mirdza Sirlaks-f-Jan. 17, 1916-Cesis, Latvia--Montreal, Canada / Biruta Balks--F--June 3, 1919--Cesis, Latvia--Rockford, Ohio
cites.note: Declaration No. 132, Celina, Ohio, 14 Aug 1950: housewife, 65, widowed; 5 ft 1 in, 170 lb, gray eyes, gray hair. Three children listed: Elvira Danenbergs (Riga, Jan 1912); Mirdza Sirlaks (17 Jan 1916, Cēsis, then in Montreal); Biruta Balks (3 Jun 1919, Cēsis, Rockford). Same ship, port and date as Arvīds. Certification A-7219632. The family memory is that she was born in Vecrauna. "Branti" may be a homestead in Vecrauna/Rauna parish. Unverified.
cites.why: The children, dates and ship all interlock with the other declarations and the census.

cites.title: Rauna births 1886 no. 33
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, img 311 (right page)
cites.quote: 1885 December fünf u. zwanzig[sten] abends 9 U. | zweiten | 33 Lubar, Lj. Luhzmann[?] / Emma Smukkul / Elt. Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. d. Marie geb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch / Tf. Md. Juhle Meeschit[?], Md. Leene Leepin[?], Jg. August Meeschit[?]
cites.translation: 1885 December twenty-fifth, 9 in the evening | [baptised on the] second | No. 33, Lubar[?], [farm] Luhzmann[?] / Emma Smukkul / parents: farmhand (Knecht) Dahw Smukkul and his wife Marie née Kahjon, both Lutheran / godparents: maid Juhle Meeschit[?], maid Leene Leepin[?], young man August Meeschit[?]
cites.note: Born 25 Dec 1885 (Julian), 9 p.m. = 6 Jan 1886 (Gregorian). Baptised 2 Feb 1886 (Julian) = 14 Feb 1886 (Gregorian): the baptism column has 'zweiten' directly beneath entry no. 32's 'Februar zweiten' (img/sf-rauna-1886-dz31-33-dates.jpg). Entry is in the 1886 register.
cites.why: Child's name, both parents (Dahw Smukkul + Marie geb. Kahjon = DP card 'Dāvis Smukuls, Marija Kajans[?]') and day/month (6 Jan Gregorian) all match the Arolsen DP card. The DP card's year 1885 is the Julian birth year. The 1947 '6.6.85 Branti' reading is therefore wrong or garbled; Branti is not named here.

cites.title: Marriage (1911) and baptism of Elvīra Sirlaka (1912) at Rīga St Martin's, Torņakalns
cites.repository: LVVA Raduraksti & Elvīra Danenberga memoir
cites.quote: The first two years of my life were spent in Torņukalns (Tower Hill), a suburb of Rīga. My father, Mārtinš Sirlaks, and my mother Emma Smukulis were both born about 8 km from each other: my mother in Vecrauna (Old Rauna) and my father in Jaunrauna (New Rauna). … At first they both worked in menial jobs, but then my father opened a tavern while mother stayed at home as a housewife. When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga to escape the anticipated disruptions and disturbances of war and went to Cēsis
cites.note: Married Mārtiņš Vilhelms Sirlaks at St Martin's Lutheran church in Torņakalns, Rīga on 22 April 1911 Jul. (5 May 1911 Greg.), had their first daughter Elvīra there on 27 December 1911 Jul. (9 January 1912 Greg., baptised at St Martin's on 19 Feb / 3 Mar 1912), and lived in Torņakalns while her husband kept a tavern until World War I broke out in 1914.

cites.title: Move from Torņakalns to Vinterkalns outside Cēsis (1914–1919)
cites.repository: Elvīra Danenberga memoir
cites.quote: When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga to escape the anticipated disruptions and disturbances of war and went to Cēsis … At first we lived in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area, several km outside of Cēsis. … Mirdza was born in this house. My mother (Māte) fed her cream of wheat
cites.note: Left Rīga at the outbreak of World War I in 1914 and lived first in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area outside Cēsis, where her second daughter Mirdza was born on 17 January 1916, before buying the house at Lielā Katrīnas iela 13 in Cēsis by 1919.

cites.translation: The family of six includes Arvids Danenbergs, 36, his wife, Elvira, 37, their three children, Peter, 6, a set of twins, Liga and Kalvis, 2 1/2, and Mrs. Danenbergs's mother, Mrs. Emma Sirlaks.
cites.note: Residing at the tenant house on the D. R. Smalley farm in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio, after arriving from Bremerhaven aboard the U.S. Army Transport Gen. Blatchford with her daughter Elvira Danenbergs, son-in-law Arvids Danenbergs, and grandchildren Peter, Liga, and Kalvis, caring for the children while Arvids and Elvira worked on the farm.
cites.why: Named as mother of Elvira Danenbergs ('Mrs. Danenberg's mother, Mrs. Emma Sirlaks') and pictured at the Smalley farm in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio.

cites.title: Household of Arwids F Danenbergs, Liberty Township, Mercer, Ohio
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: Emma Sirlaks: Race = White; Birth 1885 @ Latvia; Residence 1949; Census 10 April 1950 @ Liberty Township, Mercer, Ohio, United States; RelationshipToHead=Mother-in-law; Age=65
cites.note: After arriving in Boston on 7 July 1949, she lived with the Danenberg family (and from early 1950 the Balks family) on the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk (and D. R. Smalley Farms, Rockford post office) in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio, where she was enumerated in the 10 April 1950 US Census and swore her Declaration of Intention in Celina on 14 August 1950.

cites.title: Move from the Rockford farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio
cites.repository: Elvīra Danenberga memoir & R. L. Polk Tiffin City Directories
cites.quote: Labos Hawkus pievīlām pēc gada aiziedami uz Tiffinu,Ohio. … Uzaudzināja ne vien Pēteri un Ilzi,bet arī dvīņus (Cvinīšus,kā viņa sauca).Pateicoties mātei mēs ar Rūtu varējām strādāt,jo bija kas uzmana mazos.
cites.translation: We let the good Hawks down after a year by leaving for Tiffin, Ohio. … She raised not only Pēteris and Ilze, but also the twins ('Cvinīši', as she called them). Thanks to mother, Rūta and I were able to work, because there was someone to watch the little ones.
cites.note: Moved with the Danenberg family after about a year on the Hawk farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (where Elvīra and Arvīds are recorded at 23 Apple Street in 1953 and on their Rural Delivery 2 Tiffin farm in 1956–1959 R. L. Polk city directories), helping raise Pēteris, Ilze, and the twins Kalvis and Līga while her daughters worked.

cites.title: S-fs-JRNP-MMG
cites.repository: FamilySearch
cites.quote: Emma Sirlaks; Death Oct 1970 Southfield, Oakland, Michigan; Birth 06 Jan 1885; age 85; ZIP 48075; issued Ohio
cites.note: SSDI: born 06 Jan 1885, died Oct 1970, age 85, last residence ZIP 48075 (Southfield), card issued in Ohio. Find a Grave has an "Emma Sirlaks", 1885-1970, age 85, buried in Toronto, Ontario (memorial 276607686), in the same Toronto index as "Mirdza Augeste Gailitis" (1916-2010, memorial 276580240). That is plausibly a burial with her daughter Mirdza's family. There is also an A-file index entry (United States, Index to Alien Case Files, 6FYW-F2RM), so a USCIS/NARA A-file exists.
cites.why: The SSDI birth date matches the declaration exactly. The Toronto burial is linked only by name, years and age.

cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan - pēdējos gados - Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota - matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
cites.translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85, was buried on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery. She had lived alternately in the USA, where two daughters survive with their families, and, in recent years, in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several serious operations, losing first one leg and, two years ago, the other to amputation.
cites.note: Aged 85, so born about 1885. She spent her old age alternately in the USA, where two of her daughters lived with their families, and (latterly) in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law Fricis Gailītis, a mathematics teacher who died in September 1969. She had had both legs amputated over the preceding years.
cites.why: Two independent notices; 'two daughters in the USA' (Elvīra and Rūta) and 'daughter Mirdza Gailīte' match the family exactly.

I certify that no prior certificate has been found for this registrant ... Filed at Seattle, Washington, on April 7, 1952
cites.note: Delayed certificate filed 7 Apr 1952 (Vol. 26, State File No. 342). It names Winter Scott Alderson (b. Oregon, age 50) and Carrie May Newman (b. New York, age 38) as parents. Supporting evidence: (1) affidavit of Carrie May Schroeder, 18 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated'; (2) affidavit of Mrs. Lola Webster, 25 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth'; (3) Portland Public Schools transcript, 1922–1923 ('Scott Alderson', 'May Alderson'). Registrar's certification: 'no prior certificate has been found for this registrant'. Signed by Estella May Hall, sworn at Portland, 13 Mar 1952.
cites.why: Primary document for date and place. It agrees with every census (b. Washington) and with the SSDI (5 May 1916). The parentage in it rests on the adoptive family's own affidavits, and the registrar found no original certificate under the Alderson name. That is what an original filed under another name would produce.

cites.title: Toronto (news column)
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan - pēdējos gados - Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota - matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
cites.translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85, was buried on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery. She had lived alternately in the USA, where two daughters survive with their families, and, in recent years, in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several serious operations, losing first one leg and, two years ago, the other to amputation.
cites.note: Aged 85, so born about 1885. She spent her old age alternately in the USA, where two of her daughters lived with their families, and (latterly) in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law Fricis Gailītis, a mathematics teacher who died in September 1969. She had had both legs amputated over the preceding years.
cites.why: Two independent notices; 'two daughters in the USA' (Elvīra and Rūta) and 'daughter Mirdza Gailīte' match the family exactly.

notes: Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (2026) gives died 1968 and married Mirdza in 1956; ours: died Sep 1969 (Laiks, Oct 1970), married May 1955, Toronto. Lead mh-gailitis-dates.

cites.title: Genevieve Danenberg | Producer, Writer — and Genevieve Symanski | Cinematographer, Editor, Producer
cites.repository: IMDb
cites.quote: Genevieve Danenberg is known for World Cup Fever (2015) and In No Sense (2016). … Genevieve Symanski is known for Beneath Me (2016) and No Such Thing (2016).
cites.note: Film work, under both of her names, in 2015 and 2016 — five credits on three small pictures. As GENEVIEVE DANENBERG (IMDb nm7717273, "Producer, Writer"): producer and writer of "World Cup Fever" (2015, tt5280956), and associate producer of the short "In No Sense" (2016, tt5752420). The Movie Database carries the same person (person 2890089, "known as an Associate Producer"). As GENEVIEVE SYMANSKI (IMDb nm7933892, "Cinematographer, Editor, Producer"): cinematographer and producer of the short "No Such Thing" (2016, tt28642446) and editor/producer of the short "Beneath Me" (2016, tt14251732), plus one "Thanks" credit.
cites.why: Two IMDb name records, in the same two years, in the same corner of independent short film, under the two surnames she is independently documented as using (Spokeo alias "Genevieve E Danenberg"; the tree's "Genevieve Elisa Symanski Nelson"). The coincidence of name, name-variant and date is strong, but IMDb gives no photograph, birth date or location on either record, so this is a reasoned identification rather than a proved one. The only other Genevieve Danenberg found — a procurement officer at Mildura Base Public Hospital in Australia — is clearly a different person and is ruled out in raw/.

cites.title: Relationship between neutrophil lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and MDSC concentration… — author affiliations
cites.repository: American Society of Clinical Oncology (ascopubs.org)
cites.quote: Genevieve Danenberg — USC Keck School of Medicine Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center, Los Angeles, CA;
cites.note: Co-author of a cancer-research abstract at the 2018 ASCO Genitourinary Cancers Symposium, with the affiliation "USC Keck School of Medicine Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center, Los Angeles, CA" — the same institution where her former father-in-law Peter V. Danenberg has been a professor since 1976. Basu A, Kollengode KA, Rafatnia A, Manoli H, **Danenberg G**, Chakravartty E, Epstein AL, Pinski JK, "Relationship between neutrophil lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and MDSC concentration in localized and metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) patients", J Clin Oncol 36, no. 6_suppl (2018): 338. The work measured myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the blood of 58 prostate-cancer patients in Jacek Pinski's group.
cites.why: Danenberg is a rare surname; the institution is precisely the one her married family belongs to; she is independently documented as having used the name "Genevieve E Danenberg" and as living in Alhambra, Altadena and Monrovia, all within a few miles of the Norris Center. But the abstract gives only "Genevieve Danenberg" with no initial or identifier, and this is the only scientific record under that name, so it is not proved. Peter can settle it in a sentence.

cites.title: NUMIDENT and 1949 Washington death record of Grover Cleveland Newman, 1901 BC marriage of Lilly E. Newman, and 1892 elopement from Fossil
cites.repository: FamilySearch / NARA, Washington State Board of Health & BC Archives
cites.quote: "value" : "\"United States, Social Security Numerical Identification Files (NUMIDENT), 1936-2007\", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6KW1-MWLZ : Fri Jul 03 20:52:03 UTC 2026), Entry for Grover Cleveland Newman and Edward Newman." … "original" : "28 Apr 1887" … "original" : "Fossil Wheel*, Oregon, United States" … "fullText" : "Grover Cleveland Newman"
cites.note: Born 28 April 1886 or 28 April 1887 in Fossil, Gilliam (later Wheeler) County, Oregon to Edward Newman and Harriet M. Brate: his September 1937 Social Security NUMIDENT application (6KW1-MWL6, SSN 539-10-1528) gives '28 Apr 1887' at 'Fossil Wheel*, Oregon, United States' (Wheeler County was created from Gilliam, Grant, and Crook counties on 17 February 1899 with Fossil as county seat), whereas the 1900 US census (MMPL-98T) gives 'Apr 1886' in 'Oregon' (age 14y) and his 1949 Washington death record (HV8L-SSN2, cn 16013) gives '28 Apr 1886' at 'Fossil, Oregon' (age 63).
cites.why: Both his signed 1937 Social Security NUMIDENT application (6KW1-MWL6) and his 1949 Washington death record (HV8L-SSN2) give his birthday and birthplace as 28 April in Fossil, Oregon, differing by one year (1887 vs. 1886, with the 1900 census MMPL-98T supporting April 1886).

cites.title: Certificate of Death: Irene Mary Meyer (1971); Certificate of Marriage: Henry L. Meyer and Irene Larson (1960); 1900 Census: Irene M Barnhart
cites.repository: Washington State Digital Archives; FamilySearch
cites.locator: WA Death Certificate State File No. 4576, Local File No. 71-86; Whatcom Co. Marriage Certificate No. 27287; 1900 Census Delta Precinct, Whatcom Co., Sheet 12A, Household 218
cites.quote: STATE FILE NUMBER 4576 | 1. DECEASED—NAME: IRENE MARY MEYER | 2. SEX: Female | 3. DATE OF DEATH: Feb. 15, 1971 | 5a. AGE—LAST BIRTHDAY: 70 | 6. DATE OF BIRTH: Aug. 16, 1900 | 8. STATE OF BIRTH: Washington | 15. FATHER—NAME: Phillip Barnhart | 16. MOTHER—MAIDEN NAME: Millie H. Walker || NO. 27287 ... Irene Larson (Female) (Place of Birth) Lynden, Wash. (Age last Birthday) Legal of Bellingham, Wash. || Irene M Barnhart, Daughter, Single, White, Age 1y, Birth Aug 1899, Washington
cites.note: Born at Lynden, Whatcom County, Washington, daughter of Phillip Grant Barnhart and Margaret Amelia Walker. Her 1971 Washington death certificate (State File No. 4576, informant husband Henry L. Meyer) gives her birth date as 'Aug. 16, 1900' and birthplace 'Washington'; her 1960 Whatcom County marriage certificate (No. 27287) and her son Charles L. Meyer's 1948 death certificate (State File No. 18626) give her birthplace as 'Lynden, Wash.' / 'Linden, Washington'; her Woodlawn Cemetery headstone and Find a Grave memorial 8580575 give 16 Aug 1900 (1900–1971); and the 1910, 1920, and 1950 censuses all give her birth year as 1900. Note: in the 1900 US Census of Delta Precinct, Whatcom County (taken June 1900, ARK 1:1:MM5M-3MV), she is already enumerated as 'Irene M Barnhart', daughter, age '1y', born 'Aug 1899' in Washington—which would make her 16 years 8 months old in May 1916 and 17 years 7 months old when her age was recorded as '17 years' on her 17 March 1917 marriage certificate.
cites.why: Her 1971 death certificate, 1960 marriage certificate, son's 1948 death certificate, headstone, and adult censuses agree on 16 Aug 1900 and Lynden, Whatcom County, Washington; the June 1900 census entry ('Aug 1899') shows she may actually have been born 16 Aug 1899.
cites.as_recorded: IRENE MARY MEYER (1971 death certificate); Irene Larson, Place of Birth: Lynden, Wash. (1960 marriage certificate); Irene M Barnhart, Birth Aug 1899 Washington (1900 census)

cites.translation: Phil. G. Barnhart Killed by Lightning. One of the severest electrical storms ever known in this section occurred last evening about dark, and was followed by rain throughout the night. Mr. Phil. G. Barnhart, living at Northwood, while engaged at work about the cream separator at his home was struck by a bolt of lightning, and almost instantly killed, dying before Dr. Mulder, who was summoned, could reach him. Mr. Barnhart was an old resident, having lived here more than twenty years, and was the father of a large family. He was an estimable citizen, honored and respected, and his sudden and unfortunate death will be a shock to his many friends. A curious incident is that some six years ago, during a much less severe electrical storm than that of last evening, Mr. Barnhart's barn was struck by lightning, set on fire, and it and its contents totally destroyed.
cites.note: Death of her father Phillip G. Barnhart at Northwood (northeast of Lynden, Whatcom County, Washington) on the evening of Wednesday, 19 June 1912: while engaged at work about the cream separator at his home during a severe electrical storm about dark, he was struck by a bolt of lightning and almost instantly killed, dying before Dr. Mulder could reach him (six years after his barn had been struck by lightning and burned); he had lived in the district for more than twenty years and was a member of Lynden Lodge No. 140, Fraternal Union of America, which passed formal resolutions of condolence on 2 July 1912.

DECEASED—NAME: IRENE MARY MEYER | 3. DATE OF DEATH: Feb. 15, 1971 | 6. DATE OF BIRTH: Aug. 16, 1900 | 15. FATHER—NAME: Phillip Barnhart | 16. MOTHER—MAIDEN NAME: Millie H. Walker
cites.note: Daughter of Phillip Grant Barnhart (1863–1912) and Margaret Amelia Walker (1869–1940), who was a daughter of William Alexander Walker and Jean (Jenette / Jane R.) Arbuckle. Proposed identification of 'Irene Barns', mother of Phillis May Barns (born 5 May 1916, Seattle): Irene Mary Barnhart (FS LB8P-85J), born at Lynden, Whatcom Co., WA (16 Aug 1900 on her 1971 death certificate and headstone; enumerated in the June 1900 census as born Aug 1899); died 15 Feb 1971 at Bellingham, Whatcom Co. Her 1917 Whatcom County marriage certificate (License No. 3201, witnessed by her mother 'Marguerit Pym') names her parents as 'Phil Barnhardt' (born Iowa) and 'Margaret Walker' (born St Louis Mo), and her 1971 Washington death certificate (State File No. 4576, informant husband Henry L. Meyer) names her parents as 'Phillip Barnhart' and 'Millie H. Walker'. Her youngest sister Phillis (Phyllis) Barnhart was born in 1908.
cites.why: Primary 1917 marriage certificate (witnessed by her mother Marguerit Pym) and 1971 death certificate both name her parents as Phil/Phillip Barnhardt/Barnhart and Margaret/Millie H. Walker, and her mother's 1940 death certificate (State File No. 246) names Margaret's parents as William A. Walker and Jenette Arbuckle. As a candidate for 'Irene Barns': 'Barns' is a short form of Barnhart; the child's name ('Phillis May Barns') echoes Irene's late father Phil and her youngest sister Phillis (born 1908); she is the only unmarried Walker–Arbuckle granddaughter of childbearing age in Washington in May 1916; and her matriline (Barnhart ← Walker ← Arbuckle ← McNiven) matches Estella's H1c114 mtDNA and Peter's autosomal matches descending from four other children of William Alexander Walker and Jean Arbuckle (names in research/ftdna/).

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.
cites.as_recorded: Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi, 2. Jahn, 3. Dahw

cites.translation: 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28 then, 35 now; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2. His wife Anne, 21; daughter Anne, 5.
cites.note: 1857 soul revision, family 10/58, XIX Gibboi farm, under 'Jahns Söhne': '2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?]' (farmer's assistant[?]), 28 at the last revision (1850), now 35 (b. c. 1822); 'dessen Sohn Marz, 1855 nachgeboren, 2' (his son Mārcis, b. 1855); 'dessen Frau Anne', 21 (b. c. 1836). With them his brother Mārcis, the farmer (41½), and 'Tochter Anne', 5, entered after Jahn's wife. Raimonds's tree has Jānis b. 1822 and his wife Anna b. 1829: her age here does not fit 1829, so she is a second wife or the tree's year is off.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3); high for Jahn (Raimonds's Jānis b. 1822, son of Jānis: age and father agree), medium for his wife: the tree's Anna b. 1829 is seven years older than this Anne.

cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti

cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 133, ff. 131v–132r), farm XVI. Pohding, family no. 28: farmer Marz Gibboi ('Marz Gibboi Wirth | aus N XXI | 27'), transferred from No. XXI Schwigur, age 27 in 1834; his son Jahn ('dessen Sohn Jahn | nachher geboren 1831 | 3', who died in 1844 per the 1850 revision); his 1st wife Marri ('dessen Frau Marri | 43'); three stepdaughters from Marri's first marriage to Jakob Pohding (1. cites.title: Obituary of Velta Grislis (beloved wife of the late Janis), St. Catharines, Ontario, and death record of Jānis Grīslis (1 Apr 2012)
cites.repository: Dignity Memorial (Hulse & English Funeral Home, St. Catharines) & Raimonds Voroņins MyHeritage tree
cites.quote: Grislis, Velta. Peacefully on Thursday, March 12th, 2015 at Tufford Manor Nursing Home in her 97th year. Velta, beloved wife of the late Janis. Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family.
cites.note: Born 19 Sep 1918; in her 97th year. 'Beloved wife of the late Janis' (Jānis Grīslis, 11 Mar 1916 – 1 Apr 2012, per a Dignity Memorial index; Timenote gives d. 01.04.2012). 'Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family': relationship not stated, a living third party. The obituary does not name her parents, but Timenote names her father Dāvis and maiden name Sirlaka, and gives her burial at Jaunrauna cemetery (ashes presumably returned to Latvia). She was a Red Cross-trained nurse: there is a 1955 file 'Grislis, Velta (Nee Sirlaks)' in the International Council of Nurses Nurse Refugee Files at the University of Pennsylvania, and Sirlaks hits in the Latvian Red Cross nurses' journal (Žēlsirdīgā Māsa, 1939–40). Her full name was Velta Skaidrīte.
cites.why: The birth year 1918, the 'late Janis' and Ontario all match the 1955 Hamilton marriage and Timenote.

cites.title: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) soul revision 1834, XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family 4 (Sillak)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: [XXIX. Leis-Sparing] / ... / 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben | — / deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof | — / " 2 " Marz | nachher geb. | — | 12. / " 3 " Jahn | nachher geb. | — | 4. ‖ 4. | Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.
cites.translation: [XXIX. Lejas-Spāriņi]: ... Family 4: Sillak Jahn, Ansche's son, manor weaver, from the manor people, died in 1830; his 1st son Dawe, ditto, 1829 to Lindenhof [Liepa] estate; 2nd son Marz, born since, 12; 3rd son Jahn, born since, 4. Sillak Masche, Ansche's daughter, his wife, 59.
cites.note: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) 8th soul revision (1834, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 112), farm XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family no. 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben' (manor weaver, came from the manor people, where in the 1826 surname revision on image 58 he was listed as 'IV. Sirlack | Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | 1825 v. Gute Wesselshof zugekommen | 47'; died in 1830); his 1st son Dawe ('deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof' — moved in 1829 to Liepa / Lindenhof manor, where he later appears as churchwarden 'Kirchenvorm. Dahwis Sillak' in 1859–62); his 2nd son Marz ('2 Sohn Marz | nachher geb. | 12', born c. 1822 — our ancestor Mārcis Sirlaks, who moved from No. XXIX Leis-Sparing to No. XIV Wihstuz and fathered Pēteris Sirlaks in 1847); his 3rd son Jahn ('3 Sohn Jahn | nachher geb. | 4', born c. 1830 — who also moved from No. XXIX to No. XIV Wihstuz by 1850, age 20); and his widow 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.' (matching her age 51 in 1826 + 8 = 59).
cites.why: Proves that Mārcis Sirlaks (b. c. 1822, father of Pēteris Sirlaks 1847–1896 at XIV. Wihstuz, recorded in 1850 as 'Marz Sillak, Jahns Sohn, aus No. XXIX') is the 2nd son of 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn' (who came to Jaunrauna from Wesselshof / Veselauska in 1825 and died in 1830 at XXIX. Leis-Sparing) × 'Masche, Ansche Tochter', and NOT the son of the other 'IV. Sirlack' head of household 'Jahn, Martz Sohn, Hofsknecht' (who died in 1821 leaving only son Peter b. c. 1814).
cites.as_recorded: 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber (1830 gestorben); deßen 1 Sohn Dawe; 2 Sohn Marz; 3 Sohn Jahn; Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau

cites.title: Purchase of Kalna Vīstuči in 1869 by Jānis Sirlaks
cites.repository: Aina Jurciņa (née Sirlaka) memoir
cites.quote: Viens no brāļiem Jānis Sirlaks 1869.gadā nopirka māju no Mārča Vīstuča. … Brāļa Jāņa māja- “Kalna Vīstuči”, brāļa Mārča- “Lejas Vīstuči”, vēlākā Dāvja māja. … Jān Sirlak dz.8.maijā 1829.gadā / mir.20.februārī 1901.gadā
cites.note: Bought the Kalna Vīstuči homestead on the Jaunrauna estate from Mārcis Vīstucis in 1869 (while his nephew Pēteris Sirlaks bought Lejas Vīstuči from von Pander on installments in 1872) and farmed Kalna Vīstuči until his death on 20 February / 5 March 1901.

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1816, manor people
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31 (fol. 26); farm 29 on image 54 (fol. 49)
cites.quote: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29 | 32. | 37. / Sohn Dawe, nachhergeboren | ½ — Jahns Eheweib Masche, Ansch T. 41
cites.translation: Weaver Jahn, son of Ansis, from no. 29, 32 [in 1811], 37 [now]; son Dāvis, born since, ½. Jahn's wife Masche, daughter of Ansis, 41.
cites.note: 1816 revision (7th), manor people: weaver Jahn, son of Ansch (Ansis), from farm no. 29, aged 32 in 1811 and 37 in 1816 (b. c. 1779); son Dawe, born after 1811, ½. Wife Masche, daughter of Ansch, 41 (b. c. 1775); daughters Trine 16, Anne 14, Marri 10, Liese 5. No surname yet (surnames were assigned in Livonia c. 1822–1826). Also on farm 29 (image 54): farmhand Jahn son of Ansch 'in B', son Peter d. 1814; and young Jahn son of Ansch 'in No. 20'. Died 1830[?] per the 1834 list.
cites.why: Identification with the 1834 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' rests on the same name and patronymic, a wife Masche daughter of Ansch in both lists (41 → 59, exactly +18 years), son Dawe born after 1811, the trade (weaver) and origin farm 29. Without a surname, a second Jahn son of Ansch on the same estate leaves some doubt.

cites.title: Extracting RNA from Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Tissue — University of Southern California
cites.repository: AUTM (Association of University Technology Managers)
cites.quote: The method of extracting RNA from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues was developed in 2000 by University of Southern California researchers Kathleen Danenberg, Ph.D., Peter Danenberg, Ph.D. and Stephen Swenson, Ph.D. … Response Genetics, a biotechnology company in Los Angeles, holds the exclusive license and has invested approximately $13 million to further develop the process.
cites.note: The invention her career turns on. With her husband Peter V. Danenberg and Stephen (Steven) Swenson, she devised a way to get usable RNA out of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue — the way hospital pathology archives store tumour samples. Until then RNA could only be had from fresh-frozen tissue, so decades of archived tumours were genetically unreadable. USC licensed it exclusively to Response Genetics, which put about $13 million into developing it; partners included Hitachi, GlaxoSmithKline, Roche and Eli Lilly. AUTM, the technology-transfer association, chose it for its Better World Project in 2008 as an invention that changed practice. Patent priority 20 Dec 1999 / 1 Dec 2000.
cites.why: Three independent sources — the patents themselves, AUTM's case study and the company's SEC filings — give the same invention, the same inventors and the same institution.

Danenberg and Steven Swenson, USC, 2011); US 8,026,062 B2 (2011); US 8,323,890 B2 (high-throughput DNA methylation analysis, USC, 2012); US 8,586,311 B2 (ERCC1 and TS expression, 2013).

cites.title: Cēsis rural birth register 1855, entry no. 214 (Kristine Gibboij)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: [Dec.] einunddreißigste Morg 7 Uhr | [Januar] sechste z. H. get. | 214. Freudenberg K. Pohding Kristine Gibboij El: Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. Wb. Anne, luth Tf. W. Gibboij Jahnis Sarriht u. Dahwis Sarriht. W. Gibboij M. Marie Sarriht
cites.translation: [December] 31st, 7 a.m. | [January] 6th, baptised at home | No. 214, Freudenberg Kalna-Podiņi: Kristine Gibboij. Parents: farmhand Mahrzis Gibboij and his wife Anne, Lutheran. Godparents: Vec-Ģiboli Jahnis Sarriht and Dahwis Sarriht, Vec-Ģiboli maid Marie Sarriht.
cites.note: Cēsis rural Lutheran birth register 1855, entry no. 214 (legitimate female no. 106): Kristine Gibboij, born 31 December 1855 O.S. at 7 a.m. (= 12 January 1856 N.S.) at Freudenberg Kalna-Podiņi ('Freudenberg K. Pohding'), baptised at home ('z. H. get.') on 6 January 1856 O.S. (= 18 January 1856 N.S.). Parents: farmhand Mahrzis Gibboij and his wife Anne, Lutheran ('El: Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. Wb. Anne, luth'). Godparents: Jahnis Sarriht and Dahwis Sarriht of Vec-Ģiboli, and maid Marie Sarriht of Vec-Ģiboli ('Tf. W. Gibboij Jahnis Sarriht u. Dahwis Sarriht. W. Gibboij M. Marie Sarriht'). Because she was born on the very last day of 1855 Old Style (12 January 1856 New Style) and baptised in January 1856, she matches both '2. Kristine, 2' in the November 1857 Priekuļi soul revision of Mārcis Ģibols (age 50) × Anne (age 38) at Rauguļi AND the Kristīne Ģibola (b. c. 1856) who married Jānis Kārnītis in Rauna on 20 June 1882 at age 26.
cites.why: Resolves Kristīne Ģibola's primary birth record and explains why the 1857 revision gives her age as 2 (born end of 1855 O.S.) while her 1882 marriage entry gives her age as 26 (born Jan 1856 N.S. / baptised Jan 1856 O.S.).

cites.title: Ainas Sirlakas atmiņas ("Vīstuči"), Aina Jurciņa née Sirlaka, Priekuļi, 1998
cites.repository: family papers (Raimonds Voroņins, 2026-10-24)
cites.locator: p. 9, section "PAR PĒTERA UN MARIJAS SESTO BĒRNU KRISTĪNI"
cites.quote: Un atzīme, ka kristīta tā paša gada otrās Lieldienās 25.aprīlī.
cites.translation: And a note that she was baptised on the second day of Easter of the same year, 25 April.
cites.note: Julian Easter 1888 fell on 24 April, so Easter Monday = 25 April Julian (= 7 May Gregorian). This proves Aina copied Julian church-book dates. "Par Kristīni tuvāku ziņu nav." In 1919 she ran across the meadows to Liepa to tell the Latvian army where the Germans were and was given a silver thaler (p. 9).
cites.why: Internally consistent with the Julian Easter of 1888: the note was clearly copied from a church-book entry.
