people.name: Līze Mežciema

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 58 | — | 68 / XIV Meschzeem | Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn | 30 | — | 40 / Marz des Jahns 1te Sohn | 6 | — | 16 / Jahn ,, 2te Sohn | 2½ | — | 12½ ‖ XIV Meschzeem | Masche deßen Weib | 50 / XIV Meschzeem | Liese deßen Weib | 40 / Mareet ihre 1te Tochter | 14½ / Anne ihre 2te Tochter | 4
cites.translation: Surname XIV Meschzeem: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 58 -> 68; his wife Masche, 50. Jahn, Jacob's 1st son, 30 -> 40; his wife Liese, 40; Jahn's 1st son Marz, 6 -> 16; 2nd son Jahn, 2½ -> 12½; their 1st daughter Mareet, 14½; their 2nd daughter Anne, 4.
cites.note: Age 40 in 1826 and 47 in 1834 at Farm 1. / I. Meschzeem, Priekuļi (born c. 1786/87).
cites.why: Consistent ages in the 1826 and 1834 Priekuļi soul revisions.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1834, I. Meschzeem, family 1
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1. | Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth | 58 | 1832 gestorben | — / dessen Sohn 1 Jahn | 29 | 1833 gestorben | — / dessen Söhne 1 Marz | 6 | — | 24 / 2 Jahn | 2½ | — | 20½ / 2 Dawe | 16 | vide N XXVIII | — / 3 Jakob jetziger Wirth | 2½ | — | 20½ ‖ 1 | dessen Wittwe Masche | 57 / dessen Wittwe Lihse | 47 / dessen Frau Babbe | 22 / dessen Töchter 1 Mareet | 21½ / 2 Anne | 11
cites.translation: Family 1: Jakob Meschzeem, former farmer, 58 [in 1816], died in 1832; his widow Masche, 57. His 1st son Jahn, 29 [in 1816], died in 1833; his widow Lihse, 47. His [Jahn's] sons: 1. Marz, 6 -> 24 (his wife Babbe, 22); 2. Jahn, 2½ -> 20½; his [Jahn's] daughters: 1. Mareet, 21½; 2. Anne, 11. [Jakob Sr.'s sons:] 2. Dawe, 16, see No. XXVIII; 3. Jakob, current farmer, 2½ -> 20½.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 117, ff. 115v–116r), farm I. Meschzeem, family no. 1: former farmer Jakob Meschzeem ('Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, died in 1832 ('1832 gestorben'), leaving widow Masche, age 57; his 1st son Jahn ('dessen Sohn 1 Jahn'), age 29 in 1816, died in 1833 ('1833 gestorben'), leaving widow Lihse, age 47; Jahn's sons 1. Marz (6 -> 24; wife Babbe, 22) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 20½); Jahn's daughters 1. Mareet (21½) and 2. Anne (11, born c. 1822/23). Jakob's 3rd son Jakob (2½ -> 20½) is now the current farmer ('3 Jakob jetziger Wirth').
cites.why: Records the exact death years of Anne Meschzeem's grandfather Jēkabs Mežciems (died 1832) and father Jānis Mežciems (died 1833), and shows 11-year-old Anne Meschzeem with her widowed mother Līze (47) and grandmother Maža (57) at I. Meschzeem.
cites.as_recorded: 1. Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth (1832 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Masche; dessen Sohn 1 Jahn (1833 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Lihse; dessen Töchter 1 Mareet, 2 Anne

notes: Mother of Anna Mežciema (I1021) and wife of Jānis Mežciems (I1412) at Farm No. 1 Meschzeem, Priekuļi (age 40 in 1826, widow age 47 in 1834, LVVA 199/1/112).

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1811, No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 6 Gibboy Gesinde / Ansche 1ster Wirth | 53 | gestorben im Jahr 1805 | — / deßen Söhne 1, Martz Wirth | 20 | — | 36 / ... / Laur | 46 | — | 62 / deßen Sohn Jahn | 6 | — | 22 / Peter | 30 | — | 46 / deßen Sohn Martz | — | nachher gebohren | 5
cites.translation: No. 6 Gibboy farm: Ansche, 1st farmer, 53 [in 1795], died in 1805; his sons: 1. Martz, farmer, 20 -> 36 ... Laur, 46 -> 62; his son Jahn, 6 -> 22; Peter, 30 [in 1795] -> 46 [in 1811]; his son Martz, born since, 5 [in 1811].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 6th soul revision (dated August 1811, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 9, p. 3v), farm No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde: in the first household (headed by 1st farmer Ansche, 53 in 1795, died 1805, and his son Martz Wirth, 20 -> 36, with Laur, 46 -> 62, and Laur's son Jahn, 6 -> 22) is listed farmhand Peter, age 30 in 1795, now age 46 in 1811 (born c. 1765), and his son Martz ('deßen Sohn Martz'), born after 1795 ('nachher gebohren'), age 5 in 1811 (born c. 1806).
cites.why: Earliest revision record of Mārcis Ģibols (1806/07–1882, father of Marija Ģibola) at age 5 with his father Pēteris (age 46, b. c. 1765) at the ancestral Gibboy (Ģiboli) farm.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1816, No. 21 Schwigur
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 21 Schwigur / Wirth Peter Jahn Sohn | 46 | — | 50 / ... / Knecht Martz Peters Sohn | 5 | — | 9
cites.translation: No. 21 Schwigur [Švīguļi]: Farmer Peter, Jahn's son, 46 -> 50 ... farmhand Martz, Peter's son, 5 [in 1811] -> 9 [in 1816].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 7th soul revision (1816, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 43, ff. 37v–38r), farm No. 21 Schwigur: at the bottom of the household of farmer Peter Jahn Sohn (46 -> 50) is 'Knecht Martz Peters Sohn', age 5 at the 1811 revision, now age 9 in 1816 (born c. 1806/07). In the 1826 surname revision at No. 21 Schwigur (image 75), this exact entry is assigned surname 'VII Gibboi' and cross-referenced to No. 16 Pohding ('VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn s. in No 16 | 9').
cites.why: Bridges the 5-year-old 'Martz, Peter's son' at No. 6 Gibboy in 1811 to 'Marz, Peters Sohn [VII Gibboi]' at No. 21 Schwigur -> No. 16 Pohding in 1826.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 16. Pohding / Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 29 | 1825 gestorben | — ‖ XXXI Pohdin | Marri deßen Wittwe s. unten verheirathet an Marz Gibboi / ... / VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21 | — | 19 ‖ VII Gibboi | Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob | 35
cites.translation: No. 16 Pohding [Podiņi]: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 29 [in 1816], died in 1825; [surname XXXI Pohdin] Marri, his widow, see below married to Marz Gibboi ... [surname VII Gibboi] Marz, Peter's son, farmer, from No. 21, 19; [surname VII Gibboi] Marri, his wife, see above widow of Jacob, 35.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 1826 surname revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 69, ff. 64v–65r), farm 16. Pohding: the previous farmer Jacob, Jahn's son ('Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth', age 29 in 1816) died in 1825 ('1825 gestorben'), leaving son Laur (2¾ -> 12¾), daughters Triene (10¾), Anne (8), and Marri (6), and widow Marri ('XXXI Pohdin | Marri deßen Wittwe s. unten verheirathet an Marz Gibboi'). At the bottom of the same farm, 'VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21', age 19 in 1826 (born c. 1806/07), has come from No. 21 Schwigur, married Jacob's 35-year-old widow Marri ('VII Gibboi | Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob | 35'), and become the farmer (Wirth) of 16. Pohding.
cites.why: Explains how 19-year-old Mārcis Ģibols (son of Pēteris of Ģiboli, raised at Švīguļi) became farmer (Wirth) of No. 16 Podiņi in 1825/26 by marrying the 35-year-old widow Marri of Podiņi, and why he remarried in October 1847 to Anne Meschzeem after Marri's death.
cites.as_recorded: VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21; Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 21 Schwigur / ... / VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn s. in No 16 | 9 | —
cites.translation: No. 21 Schwigur [Švīguļi]: ... [surname] VII Gibboi: Marz, Peter's son, see in No. 16 [Pohding], 9 [in 1816].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 1826 surname revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 75, ff. 70v–71r), farm 21 Schwigur: 'VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn s. in No 16 | 9 | —', recording that Martz, Peter's son (age 9 at No. 21 Schwigur in the 1816 revision), took surname No. VII Gibboi and moved to No. 16 Pohding.
cites.why: Direct cross-reference linking the 9-year-old orphan 'Knecht Martz Peters Sohn' at No. 21 Schwigur in 1816 to the 19-year-old farmer 'VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21' at No. 16 Pohding in 1826.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1834, XVI. Pohding, family 28 (Marz Gibboi Wirth)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 28 | Marz Gibboi Wirth | — | aus N XXI | 27 / dessen Sohn Jahn | — | nachher geboren 1831 | 3 ‖ 28 | dessen Frau Marri | 43 / dessen Töchter 1 Trihne | 18¾ / 2 Anne | 15 / 3 Marri | 13 / 4 Lihse | 7 / 5 Mahde | 5 / 6 Kristine | ¼
cites.translation: Family 28: Marz Gibboi, farmer, from No. XXI, 27; his son Jahn, born after [in] 1831, 3. His wife Marri, 43; daughters: 1. Trihne, 18¾; 2. Anne, 15; 3. Marri, 13; 4. Lihse, 7; 5. Mahde, 5; 6. Kristine, ¼.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 133, ff. 131v–132r), farm XVI. Pohding, family no. 28: farmer Marz Gibboi ('Marz Gibboi Wirth | aus N XXI | 27'), transferred from No. XXI Schwigur, age 27 in 1834; his son Jahn ('dessen Sohn Jahn | nachher geboren 1831 | 3', who died in 1844 per the 1850 revision); his 1st wife Marri ('dessen Frau Marri | 43'); three stepdaughters from Marri's first marriage to Jakob Pohding (1. Trihne 18¾, 2. Anne 15, 3. Marri 13); and three daughters from his marriage to Marri (4. Lihse 7, 5. Mahde 5, 6. Kristine ¼).
cites.why: Confirms that the 'Marz Gibboi' at XVI. Pohding in 1834 (who had son Jahn b. 1831, d. 1844, and moved to XIV. Luste in 1850 and Rauguļi in 1857 with his second wife Anne) is the very same 'Marz Gibboi Wirth aus N XXI' (son of Pēteris Ansis's son of Ģiboli).

The 1857 revision settles it for the 1807 man ('Marz Gibboi 50 … Töchter 1. Marri 4, 2. Christine 2'), so his I500599 is this person, Marija's father of her 1853 baptism. cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.

cites.note: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) 8th soul revision (1834, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 112), farm XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family no. 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben' (manor weaver, came from the manor people, where in the 1826 surname revision on image 58 he was listed as 'IV. Sirlack | Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | 1825 v. Gute Wesselshof zugekommen | 47'; died in 1830); his 1st son Dawe ('deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof' — moved in 1829 to Liepa / Lindenhof manor, where he later appears as churchwarden 'Kirchenvorm. Dahwis Sillak' in 1859–62); his 2nd son Marz ('2 Sohn Marz | nachher geb. | 12', born c. 1822 — our ancestor Mārcis Sirlaks, who moved from No. XXIX Leis-Sparing to No. XIV Wihstuz and fathered Pēteris Sirlaks in 1847); his 3rd son Jahn ('3 Sohn Jahn | nachher geb. | 4', born c. 1830 — who also moved from No. XXIX to No. XIV Wihstuz by 1850, age 20); and his widow 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.' (matching her age 51 in 1826 + 8 = 59).
cites.why: Proves that Mārcis Sirlaks (b. c. 1822, father of Pēteris Sirlaks 1847–1896 at XIV. Wihstuz, recorded in 1850 as 'Marz Sillak, Jahns Sohn, aus No. XXIX') is the 2nd son of 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn' (who came to Jaunrauna from Wesselshof / Veselauska in 1825 and died in 1830 at XXIX. Leis-Sparing) × 'Masche, Ansche Tochter', and NOT the son of the other 'IV. Sirlack' head of household 'Jahn, Martz Sohn, Hofsknecht' (who died in 1821 leaving only son Peter b. c. 1814).

cites.translation: Farm No. XIV Vīstuči … family 15/95: Mārcis Sirlaks, son of Jānis, aged 28 at the last revision, 36 now; his stepson[?] Dāvis Vīstucs, 14; son Pēteris Sirlaks, 10. His wife Anne, widow of [a] Vīstucs, 51.
cites.note: 1858 revision list (10th revision), family no. 95 (9th revision no. 15). Marz Sillakk, son of Jahn: aged 28 at the 1850 revision, 36 now (so b. c. 1821/22). His stepson[?] Dahw Wihstuz: 6 → 14. Son Peter Sillakk: 2 → 10. Female side: 'his wife Anne, widowed Wihstuz', 51 (so b. c. 1806/07). So Anne was the widow of a Wihstuz (the farm's earlier family) and Dahw Wihstuz is Peter's older half-brother. Gives Pēteris's grandfather's name, Jānis (Jahn), and the patronymic of Mārcis.
cites.why: Peter, son of Marz, aged 10 at the Vīstuči farm matches the 1847 baptism of Peter, son of Mahrz Sirlakk and Anne, at Wihstuz. 'Sillakk' is the revision clerk's spelling; the family index of the same volume lists it as 'Sillak' (no. 95).

cites.title: Cēsis rural congregation births 1853, no. 149
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 4, l. 586, image 13 (right page, folio 10)
cites.quote: [August] — sechsten Morg. 8 Uhr | — sechzehnten | 149. Freudenberg K. Pohdis. Marie Gibboij. Lett. Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. W. Anne, luth. T. Lej Pohdis Jehkabs Pohdis u. s. W. Lihse, K. Pohdis Marie Bitte.
cites.translation: Born [August] the sixth, 8 a.m.; baptised the sixteenth. No. 149. Freudenberg, Upper Pohdis farm. Marie Gibboy. [Parents:] Latvian farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutheran. Godparents: from Lower Pohdis, Jēkabs Pohdis and his wife Līze; from Upper Pohdis, Marie Bitte.
cites.note: Born 6 Aug 1853 Julian (= 18 Aug 1853 Gregorian) at 8 a.m.; baptised 16 Aug 1853. Daughter of Latvian farmhand (Kn. = Knecht) Mahrzis (Mārcis) Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutherans (mother by given name only, as usual in 1853). Godparents: Jehkabs Pohdis and his wife Lihse of Lejas-Pohdis, and Marie Bitte[?] of Kalna-Pohdis. The 71st legitimate girl of the year. The same volume shows a farm named 'Gibboy' on Freudenberg (marriages 1853 no. 21), the likely origin of the surname, and the death of an unmarried maidservant Masche Gibboy, aged 58⅔, at Freudenberg Lejas-Dauksche (deaths 1853 no. 154). Kristīne Gibboy, Marie's probable sister and godmother of Mārtiņš Sirlaks in 1883, should be among later Freudenberg births (Cēsis rural Dz 1847–1879, LVVA 235/7/104).
cites.why: Given name, surname (the same 'Gibboy' spelling as her 1874 marriage and her children's baptisms), exact date of the relative's tree (6 Aug 1853, so the tree uses the Julian date) and the tree's place 'Priekuļi' (= Freudenberg) all match. Verified on the crop. Not formally linked to the 1874 bride by a stated age or parents, so 'high' rests on the coincidence of all four details.

notes: Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (I19), his note: «https://www.raduraksti.arhivi.lv/objects/1:4:11:2055:2343:17226#&gid=1&pid=93 Marija piedzima Priekuļos 93.kadrs, 149.ieraksts»

Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (I19), his note: «Priekuļos ir Ģiboļu kalns. Blakus ir arī mājas ar nosaukumu Ģibolas. Dokumentos uzvārds tiek rakstīts Gibboj, kas varētu atbilst māju un kalnu nosaukumam, tāpēc savos pierasktos izmantošu uzvārdu Ģibols.»

Raimonds's MyHeritage tree (2026) makes her the daughter of Mārcis Ģibols (b. 1816, son of Jānis and Masche) and Anna Balodis (b. 1819), married 1843: unsourced, added in 2021. The 1857 Priekuļi soul revision contradicts it: she is 'Marri, 4', daughter of Marz Gibboi (50) and his wife Anne (38) at the Rauguļi farm, with her sister Christine (2), while the 1816 Mārcis is at the Ģiboļi farm with his wife Anne and no Marija. Her parents are Mārcis b. c. 1807 × Anna b. c. 1819, his own 1807 couple (whose 1857 household his note describes), as her 1853 baptism's Mahrzis Gibboy and Anne. His 1816 couple are kept as other people, not linked to her. Lead marija-gibols-parents.

cites.title: Tavern and residence of Mārtinš Sirlaks in Torņakalns, Rīga (1911–1914)
cites.repository: LVVA Raduraksti & Elvīra Danenberga memoir
cites.quote: The first two years of my life were spent in Torņukalns (Tower Hill), a suburb of Rīga. My father, Mārtinš Sirlaks, and my mother Emma Smukulis were both born about 8 km from each other … At first they both worked in menial jobs, but then my father opened a tavern while mother stayed at home as a housewife. When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga to escape the anticipated disruptions and disturbances of war and went to Cēsis
cites.note: Married Emma Smukule at St Martin's Lutheran church in Torņakalns, Rīga on 22 April 1911 Jul. (5 May 1911 Greg.), opened a tavern in Torņakalns where their eldest daughter Elvīra spent her first two years (born 9 January 1912), and lived there until World War I broke out in 1914.

cites.title: Rented house in Vinterkalns outside Cēsis (1914–1919)
cites.repository: Elvīra Danenberga memoir
cites.quote: At first we lived in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area, several km outside of Cēsis. … Mirdza was born in this house.
cites.note: Left Rīga at the start of World War I in 1914 and lived first in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area outside Cēsis, where his second daughter Mirdza was born on 17 January 1916, before buying Lielā Katrīnas iela 13 in Cēsis by 1919.

cites.title: Baznīcas ziņas. Cēsu lauku draudze (in the article run headed 'Patiesības apliecinātāji')
cites.repository: Latvian National Library, periodika.lv
cites.quote: Baznīcas zinas. Cēsu lauka [sic] draudze. … Miruši: Mārtiņš-Vilhelms Sirlaks, 59 g. v. no Cēsīm, Mārcis Jēkabsons, 80 g. v. no Cēsu Lejas Senčiem …
cites.translation: Church news. Cēsis rural congregation. … Died: Mārtiņš-Vilhelms Sirlaks, aged 59, of Cēsis; Mārcis Jēkabsons, aged 80, …
cites.note: Aged 59, so born about 1883/84. Full name Mārtiņš-Vilhelms. His death is entered in the Cēsis RURAL congregation (Cēsu lauku draudze) news, the same register as Elvīra's 1941 wedding. Funeral 3 Jan 1943 at 2 p.m. from St John's church, Cēsis, to the Lejas kapi (Lower Cemetery), per a family death notice reproduced on Timenote. Timenote gives father Pēteris and birth year 1884. This explains why Mārtiņš was not in the 1944 flight.
cites.why: The church-news entry (name, age, Cēsis) and the family death notice (date, St John's, Lejas kapi) agree; his father Pēteris matches the tree. Note: the memoir's father 'Mārtiņš' is confirmed as 'Mārtiņš-Vilhelms'.

cites.note: Died early Sunday, 30 December 1928, at her home at 1208 Belmont Street, Portland, Oregon, of injuries suffered at midnight Friday, 28 December 1928, when she fell to the floor in her room; widow of the late Rev. Christopher P. Alderson, pioneer circuit-riding minister of the Methodist Episcopal church; born in Cook County, Illinois, 26 January 1842; crossed the plains with her parents, Mr. and Mrs. Charles Royal, in 1852, settling first at Astoria and later on a donation land claim near Gresham; survived by son W. cites.title: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) soul revision 1834, XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family 4 (Sillak)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: [XXIX. Leis-Sparing] / ... / 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben | — / deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof | — / " 2 " Marz | nachher geb. | — | 12. / " 3 " Jahn | nachher geb. | — | 4. ‖ 4. | Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.
cites.translation: [XXIX. Lejas-Spāriņi]: ... Family 4: Sillak Jahn, Ansche's son, manor weaver, from the manor people, died in 1830; his 1st son Dawe, ditto, 1829 to Lindenhof [Liepa] estate; 2nd son Marz, born since, 12; 3rd son Jahn, born since, 4. Sillak Masche, Ansche's daughter, his wife, 59.
cites.note: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) 8th soul revision (1834, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 112), farm XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family no. 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben' (manor weaver, came from the manor people, where in the 1826 surname revision on image 58 he was listed as 'IV. Sirlack | Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | 1825 v. Gute Wesselshof zugekommen | 47'; died in 1830); his 1st son Dawe ('deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof' — moved in 1829 to Liepa / Lindenhof manor, where he later appears as churchwarden 'Kirchenvorm. Dahwis Sillak' in 1859–62); his 2nd son Marz ('2 Sohn Marz | nachher geb. | 12', born c. 1822 — our ancestor Mārcis Sirlaks, who moved from No. XXIX Leis-Sparing to No. XIV Wihstuz and fathered Pēteris Sirlaks in 1847); his 3rd son Jahn ('3 Sohn Jahn | nachher geb. | 4', born c. 1830 — who also moved from No. XXIX to No. XIV Wihstuz by 1850, age 20); and his widow 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.' (matching her age 51 in 1826 + 8 = 59).
cites.why: Proves that Mārcis Sirlaks (b. c. 1822, father of Pēteris Sirlaks 1847–1896 at XIV. Wihstuz, recorded in 1850 as 'Marz Sillak, Jahns Sohn, aus No. XXIX') is the 2nd son of 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn' (who came to Jaunrauna from Wesselshof / Veselauska in 1825 and died in 1830 at XXIX. Leis-Sparing) × 'Masche, Ansche Tochter', and NOT the son of the other 'IV. Sirlack' head of household 'Jahn, Martz Sohn, Hofsknecht' (who died in 1821 leaving only son Peter b. c. 1814).
cites.as_recorded: 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber (1830 gestorben); deßen 1 Sohn Dawe; 2 Sohn Marz; 3 Sohn Jahn; Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 58 | — | 68 / XIV Meschzeem | Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn | 30 | — | 40 / Marz des Jahns 1te Sohn | 6 | — | 16 / Jahn ,, 2te Sohn | 2½ | — | 12½ ‖ XIV Meschzeem | Masche deßen Weib | 50 / XIV Meschzeem | Liese deßen Weib | 40 / Mareet ihre 1te Tochter | 14½ / Anne ihre 2te Tochter | 4
cites.translation: Surname XIV Meschzeem: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 58 -> 68; his wife Masche, 50. Jahn, Jacob's 1st son, 30 -> 40; his wife Liese, 40; Jahn's 1st son Marz, 6 -> 16; 2nd son Jahn, 2½ -> 12½; their 1st daughter Mareet, 14½; their 2nd daughter Anne, 4.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1834, I. Meschzeem, family 1
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1. | Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth | 58 | 1832 gestorben | — / dessen Sohn 1 Jahn | 29 | 1833 gestorben | — / dessen Söhne 1 Marz | 6 | — | 24 / 2 Jahn | 2½ | — | 20½ / 2 Dawe | 16 | vide N XXVIII | — / 3 Jakob jetziger Wirth | 2½ | — | 20½ ‖ 1 | dessen Wittwe Masche | 57 / dessen Wittwe Lihse | 47 / dessen Frau Babbe | 22 / dessen Töchter 1 Mareet | 21½ / 2 Anne | 11
cites.translation: Family 1: Jakob Meschzeem, former farmer, 58 [in 1816], died in 1832; his widow Masche, 57. His 1st son Jahn, 29 [in 1816], died in 1833; his widow Lihse, 47. His [Jahn's] sons: 1. Marz, 6 -> 24 (his wife Babbe, 22); 2. Jahn, 2½ -> 20½; his [Jahn's] daughters: 1. Mareet, 21½; 2. Anne, 11. [Jakob Sr.'s sons:] 2. Dawe, 16, see No. XXVIII; 3. Jakob, current farmer, 2½ -> 20½.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 117, ff. 115v–116r), farm I. Meschzeem, family no. 1: former farmer Jakob Meschzeem ('Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, died in 1832 ('1832 gestorben'), leaving widow Masche, age 57; his 1st son Jahn ('dessen Sohn 1 Jahn'), age 29 in 1816, died in 1833 ('1833 gestorben'), leaving widow Lihse, age 47; Jahn's sons 1. Marz (6 -> 24; wife Babbe, 22) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 20½); Jahn's daughters 1. Mareet (21½) and 2. Anne (11, born c. 1822/23). Jakob's 3rd son Jakob (2½ -> 20½) is now the current farmer ('3 Jakob jetziger Wirth').
cites.why: Records the exact death years of Anne Meschzeem's grandfather Jēkabs Mežciems (died 1832) and father Jānis Mežciems (died 1833), and shows 11-year-old Anne Meschzeem with her widowed mother Līze (47) and grandmother Maža (57) at I. Meschzeem.
cites.as_recorded: 1. Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth (1832 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Masche; dessen Sohn 1 Jahn (1833 gestorben); dessen Wittwe Lihse; dessen Töchter 1 Mareet, 2 Anne

notes: Paternal grandmother of Anna Mežciema (I1021) and wife of farmer Jēkabs Jāņa d. Mežciems (I1414) at Farm No. 1 Meschzeem, Priekuļi (age 50 in 1826, widow age 57 in 1834, LVVA 199/1/112).

cites.title: Beginning to end of passenger train service in Wilmington, Midland and beyond
cites.repository: Wilmington News Journal (AIM Media Midwest), wnewsj.com
cites.quote: Melinda Danenbergs' research led to this column — inspired by her interest in railroads and local history, and by the News Journal's/Clinton County History Center's January 13 Throwback Thursday photo "Bridge to Train's Past." … By Melinda Danenbergs, Contributing columnist
cites.note: Local historian and contributing columnist to the Wilmington News Journal (wnewsj.com, 1547 Rombach Avenue, Wilmington, Ohio), writing about the history of Jefferson Township, Midland, Westboro, Blanchester and Clinton County. Identified columns: "Westboro ceremony has storied history" (1 June 2017, "Submitted by Melinda Danenbergs"); "A bridge to Westboro's past" (19 February 2021, "By Melinda Danenbergs, For The News Journal"); "Beginning to end of passenger train service in Wilmington, Midland and beyond" (27 January 2022, "By Melinda Danenbergs, Contributing columnist" — "Melinda Danenbergs' research led to this column — inspired by her interest in railroads and local history"). She also writes history columns into the Facebook group "Blanchester, Ohio History and Genealogy" as "Mel Danenbergs", where another page calls her "Local historian Melinda Danenbergs".
cites.why: Signed bylines in a newspaper of record, over nine years, in the county where the voter file puts her; the subjects are her own township and village.

cites.title: Jefferson Township School Alumni & Friends gather for 103rd annual meeting
cites.repository: Wilmington News Journal (AIM Media Midwest), wnewsj.com
cites.quote: Association President Ed Pagett presided over the gathering, assisted by Vice President Laura Summers, Treasurer Darlene Kassner, and Secretary Melinda Danenbergs. … The evening's program was presented by Kassner and Danenbergs, who shared historical information and projected vintage photographs highlighting Jefferson Township, Midland City, and Westboro.
cites.note: Secretary of the Jefferson Township School Alumni & Friends association. At its 103rd annual meeting, held on Saturday 13 June 2026 in the Westboro Community Church fellowship hall, she sat with President Ed Pagett, Vice-President Laura Summers and Treasurer Darlene Kassner, and she and Kassner gave the evening's programme: "Kassner and Danenbergs… shared historical information and projected vintage photographs highlighting Jefferson Township, Midland City, and Westboro." The meeting opened with a recording of the historic Jefferson school bell rung twelve times.
cites.why: Named in office in a newspaper report of the meeting, in her own township.

cites.translation: 5000 Relatives in Missouri: Harry Norman, a St. Louis newspaper man, was in Hannibal last night returning from the funeral of his grandmother, Mrs. Emma Jane Nolen, of Monroe City, who died there Thursday. Mrs. Nolen was a pioneer of Northeast Missouri and had lived in Monroe county for nearly three-fourths of a century. With many of her relatives in Culpeper county, Virginia, she emigrated to Missouri when a child and it is probable that she is related to 5,000 persons in this section of the State principally around Monroe City, Paris and Stoutsville. She was the mother of ten children, six of whom survive her, the grandmother of twenty-six and the great-grandmother of twenty-three, twenty-one of whom survive. The surviving children are: J. H. Nolen, of Jefferson City, Deputy State Labor Commissioner; F. M. Nolen, of Paris, Sheriff of Monroe county; Oliver T. Nolen of Iola, Kas.; Ambrose J. Nolen, Melvin P. Nolen and Mrs. Mary E. Norman, of Monroe City. Mrs. Nolen, whose maiden name was Yowell, was a member of the Christian Church and the widow of John L. Nolen, a native of Hardin county, Kentucky. Her husband also was a pioneer settler of Northeast Missouri. He was one of the first shippers of live stock over the Hannibal and St. Joseph railroad.
cites.note: Death of his mother Mrs. Emma Jane (Yowell) Nolen in Monroe City, Monroe County, Missouri on Thursday, 15 July 1909; she emigrated as a child from Culpeper County, Virginia to Monroe County, Missouri (where she lived for nearly 75 years), was a member of the Christian Church, and was the widow of John L. Nolen, a native of Hardin County, Kentucky and pioneer settler of Northeast Missouri who was one of the first shippers of livestock over the Hannibal and St. Joseph Railroad; she was the mother of ten children, six of whom survived her: J. H. [John] Nolen of Jefferson City (Deputy State Labor Commissioner), F. M. [Marion] Nolen of Paris (Sheriff of Monroe County), Oliver T. Nolen of Iola, Kansas, and Ambrose J. Nolen, Melvin P. Nolen, and Mrs. Mary E. Norman of Monroe City.
cites.why: Published obituary of Mrs. Emma Jane (Yowell) Nolen in the Monroe City Democrat (22 July 1909, p. 4) naming her son Melvin P. Nolen of Monroe City, her late husband John L. Nolen, and five other surviving children.

cites.title: Obituary of Mirdza Gailīte — West Bloomfield residence
cites.repository: National Library of Latvia (periodika.lv)
cites.locator: Laiks, Nr.35 (18.09.2010), p. 22, by Vilis Kalniņš
cites.quote: No mums šķīrusies Mirdza Gailīte (dzirn. [sic: dzim.] Sirlaks) dzimusi 1916. gada 17. janvāri Vidzemes skaistajā pilsētā Cēsis. … Pēc Otrā pasaules kara liktenis ģimeni aizveda uz Kanādu. … Pēc vīra aiziešanas mūžībā kādu laiku dzīvoja Detroitas apkaimē West Bloomfield savā dzīvoklī. Viņa 1990. gada sākumā iestājās Detroitas Daugavas Vanagu apvienībā … Mirdzas divas māsas arī dzīvoja West Bloomfield un Garezera (Long Lake) apkaimē. Pēc aiziešanas pensijā Mirdza Gailīte atgriezās Vindzorā, Kanādā … Mirdza Gailīte aizgāja mūžībā pēkšņi 2010. gada 5. jūlijā. Viņu izvadīja 10. jūlijā no Anderson Funeral Home Vindzorā. Nelaiķe guldīta smilšu kalniņā Toronto.
cites.translation: Mirdza Gailīte (née Sirlaks) has left us. Born 17 January 1916 in the beautiful Vidzeme town of Cēsis. … After the Second World War fate took the family to Canada. … After her husband's death she lived for a while in her apartment in West Bloomfield, near Detroit. In early 1990 she joined the Detroit Daugavas Vanagi branch … Mirdza's two sisters also lived in West Bloomfield and near Garezers (Long Lake). After retiring Mirdza Gailīte returned to Windsor, Canada … She died suddenly on 5 July 2010. The funeral was on 10 July from Anderson Funeral Home, Windsor. She was laid to rest in Toronto.
cites.note: Elvīra's sister. The memoir says Mirdza was born at the rented house in Vinterkalns outside Cēsis, which fits.
cites.why: Obituary; maiden name Sirlaks; Cēsis; two sisters in West Bloomfield and Garezers = Rūta and Elvīra.

cites.title: Raunas latviešu draudzes 1870. gada jūlija–1876. gada dzimušo un kristīto reģistrs, 1875 no. 71
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1875 März | zwei und zwanzigsten, 8¼[?] Uhr abends | eodem die [= neunten] | No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Lijas Wihstutschi. Natalie Emilie Sirlak. V. Landesbesitzer[?] Peter Sirlak, M. Marrie geb. Gibboy, beide evang. luth. Pathen: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy, Wirth Dahw Bitte sammt[?] Katrihne. gat.[?] in d. Kirche vom Pastor loci.
cites.translation: 1875, March [page]. Born the 22nd [of February], 8:15[?] p.m.; baptised the same day as the entries above (9 March). No. 71. Ronneburg-Neuhof, Greater Vīstuči farm: Natalie Emilie Sirlak. Father: landholder[?] Peter Sirlak; mother: Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: [maid?] Kristine Gibboy, farmer Dahw Bitte with Katrihne. Baptised in the church by the parish pastor.
cites.note: Born [February] 22nd 1875 at 8¼[?] p.m.; baptised 9 March 1875 in the church by the parish pastor (Pastor loci). Parents: farm owner[?] ('Landesbesitzer'[?]) Peter Sirlak and Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy (presumably a Gibbo relative of the mother), farmer (Wirth) Dahw Bitte and [his wife] Katrihne. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1875, no. 71. The birth month is not written on this line; it is carried down from no. 66 ('Februar'). Probably the eldest child, born a year after the Feb 1874 marriage. She is not in the 2015 tree. The farm name shows that 'Lj.' in 1890 = Latvian 'Lielie' (Greater) Vīstuči. 'Wd.', used for another Vīstuči household in 1885, is probably 'Vidus' (Middle).
cites.why: Same parents' names and farm as the 1890 baptism of Anna.

cites.title: Pēteris Sirlaks
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 10.08.1847 Miršanas datums: 10.11.1896 … Tēva vārds: Mārcis … Kapsēta: Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi … Marija Sirlaka — Sieva — 00.00.1853 – 00.00.1925
cites.translation: Born 10 Aug 1847, died 10 Nov 1896; father's name Mārcis; cemetery Jaunrauna (Priekuļi parish); wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925
cites.note: Timenote gives Pēteris Sirlaks 10 Aug 1847 – 10 Nov 1896, son of Mārcis and Anna Sirlaks, buried in Jaunrauna cemetery (Priekuļu pagasts, Jaunraunas kapi). Wife Marija Sirlaka 1853–1925, NOT 1920 as in the 2015 tree. Children: Natalie 1875–1887, Ernestīne 1879, Mārtiņš 1884–1942, Dāvis 1886–1952, Kristīne 1888, Anna 1890 (the memoir's aunt Anna in Rīga), Augusts 1895. 1938 court notices (Valdības Vēstnesis) mention mortgages issued by a Pēteris Sirlaks, with inheritance shares under a 16 Apr 1915 division act going to Augusts, Ernestīne and Anna Sirlaks. Very likely the same family's farm, which would place the estate division in 1915. PROBABLE SOURCE OF THE 2015 DATES: MyHeritage 'Jurcins Web Site' by Māris Jurciņš (Latvia), whose public name index spells her 'Marija Sirlaka (Ģībojs)', 'Marija Gilboy' and 'Gibboja (Ģībojs)'. 'Gibboja' is exactly the 2015 tree's spelling. Peter emailed himself 'Sirlaks myheritage.com genealogy' on 2018-11-16. MyHeritage pages are behind an hCaptcha and were NOT opened. Marija's maiden name 'Ģībojs/Gibboja' should be verified in the Jaunrauna/Rauna church books.
cites.why: Timenote's exact dates match the 2015 tree for Pēteris; the MyHeritage spelling 'Gibboja' matches. Both are user trees without a cited record, so they are derivative until checked against the Rauna/Jaunrauna registers (Raduraksti).

cites.note: IN THE EIGHTH GRADE AT HOPEWELL-LOUDON SCHOOL, BASCOM, SENECA COUNTY, OHIO, in the school year 1955–56, in Mrs Patricia Hoffert's class. This is the first dated evidence of where the family lived in the Ohio years. Until now the only fixed point between the Boston landing of 7 July 1949 and his B.S. at Case in Cleveland in 1964 was the 1950 census, which has his father a farm hand in Liberty Township, Mercer County, in far western Ohio. Bascom is 80 miles north-east of that, south of Fostoria in Seneca County. His twin brother and sister Kalvis and Līga are in the two third-grade photographs of the same yearbook — the three grades (8, 3, 3) that their birth years (Sep 1942, Nov 1946 ×2) require. Hopewell-Loudon is a single K–12 school, so he may well have gone on to finish high school there, about 1960, before Case; that is a lead, not a fact.
cites.why: All three Danenbergs children appear in one small Ohio school's yearbook for one year, in exactly the right grades for their known ages; no other Danenbergs family is known in Ohio, and the surname has four bearers in the whole state today.

cites.quote: No 19 Gibbain / Wirth Marting Ansche Sohn | 36 | — | 40 / Marteng Sohn Jacob | 6 | — | 10 / Knecht Laure Ansche Sohn | 62 | — | 66 / Laure Sohn Jahn | 22 | — | 26 / Jahn Sohn Martze | neugebohren | ¼ / Knecht Peter Ansche Sohn | 46 | gestorben | —
cites.translation: No. 19 Gibbain [Ģiboli]: Farmer Marting, Ansche's son, 36 -> 40; Marting's son Jacob, 6 -> 10; farmhand Laure, Ansche's son, 62 -> 66; Laure's son Jahn, 22 -> 26; Jahn's son Martze, newborn, ¼; farmhand Peter, Ansche's son, 46 [in 1811], died.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 7th soul revision (1816, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 41, ff. 35v–36r), farm No. 19 Gibbain (renumbered from No. 6 Gibboy in 1811): following farmer Marting Ansche Sohn (36 -> 40) and farmhand Laure Ansche Sohn (62 -> 66) is 'Knecht Peter Ansche Sohn', age 46 at the 1811 revision, now recorded as 'gestorben' (died between 1811 and 1816). This gives Pēteris's patronymic — Ansche Sohn (son of Ansis, like Laure Ansche Sohn b. c. 1749 and 1st farmer Ansche b. c. 1742) — and explains why his orphaned 9-year-old son Martz Peters Sohn (age 5 in 1811) appears two farms over at No. 21 Schwigur in 1816.

cites.title: Building sandcastles in December
cites.repository: Palo Alto Online / Palo Alto Weekly (Embarcadero Media)
cites.quote: For the Danenberg family, it's not just about the destination it's about the experience on the way there.
cites.note: Interviewed and quoted at length in a Palo Alto Weekly feature on family winter traditions. In the summer of 2015 she drew up a to-do list of California state beaches and parks to work through with Peter and their four children, then aged three years to five months, as a weekly family tradition, and filmed each trip: "After documenting each trip by creating videos using Google Pictures, Danenberg's son seemed more receptive to having conversations about what he did each day." In her own words: "'We said, "Why don't we just get (the kids) some warmer coats and go through the list of beaches and state beaches?" Within our area there are so many different beautiful places to see. We've been doing this for about three months. We're pretty serious about it!' she said, laughing… 'I really want my kids to see these memories. There are so many ways for them to see their memories now with YouTube, photo books and stuff like that. I'm inspired to show them what they do,' she said. 'I think my husband's inspiration is (that) he wants to show them the outdoors. It makes family life more fun.'" In November 2015 the family went to Half Moon Bay, built sandcastles, hunted sand crabs and bought a Christmas tree at Santa's Village in Scotts Valley on the way home over Highway 17.
cites.why: A signed newspaper feature naming and quoting her, with her husband and four children.

cites.title: Aina Jurciņa
cites.repository: Timenote.info / Nekropole.info (CC-BY)
cites.quote: Dzimšanas datums: 00.00.1920 Miršanas datums: 18.03.2003 … Pirmslaulību (cits) uzvārds: Sirlaka … Kapsēta: Gulbene, Vecie kapi … Dāvis Sirlaks — Tēvs — 1886–1952; Alma Sirlaka — Māte — 1887–1959; Valdis Jurciņš — Dēls — 04.03.1947–04.09.2019; Alberts Jurciņš — Vīrs — 14.12.1916–1953
cites.translation: Born 1920, died 18 Mar 2003; maiden name Sirlaka; cemetery Gulbene Old Cemetery; father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952), mother Alma Sirlaka (1887–1959), son Valdis Jurciņš (1947–2019), husband Alberts Jurciņš (1916–1953)
cites.note: Identity of the memoirist. Timenote (nekropole.info) memorial pages give Aina Jurciņa, maiden name Sirlaka, born 1920, died 18 March 2003, buried in the Gulbene Old Cemetery. They name her father Dāvis Sirlaks (1886–1952) and mother Alma (1887–1959); her husband Alberts Jurciņš (b. 14 Dec 1916, d. 1953); her son Valdis Jurciņš (4 Mar 1947 – 4 Sep 2019, also Gulbene); her sisters Velta Grīslis (1918–2015) and Ilga Stangaine (1922–2011); and her brothers Valdis Sirlaks (1924–1995) and Jānis (1916–1918). So Aina is Elvīra's first cousin through Dāvis of Vīstuči, exactly as Raimonds said ('Elvīras māsīca'). Her married name JURCIŅA is the name to search in catalogues; the memoir is probably an unpublished family typescript held by her descendants (Jurciņš family, Gulbene) or by Raimonds.
cites.why: User-contributed memorial site (secondary), but internally consistent and independently corroborated by the 1942 Jelgava banns (Alberts Jurciņš × Aina Sirlaka) and by Velta's 1955 marriage and 2015 death. Not yet checked against a civil or church record.

cites.title: Obituary of Velta Grislis (beloved wife of the late Janis), St. Catharines, Ontario, and death record of Jānis Grīslis (1 Apr 2012)
cites.repository: Dignity Memorial (Hulse & English Funeral Home, St. Catharines) & Raimonds Voroņins MyHeritage tree
cites.quote: Grislis, Velta. Peacefully on Thursday, March 12th, 2015 at Tufford Manor Nursing Home in her 97th year. Velta, beloved wife of the late Janis. Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family.
cites.note: Born 19 Sep 1918; in her 97th year. 'Beloved wife of the late Janis' (Jānis Grīslis, 11 Mar 1916 – 1 Apr 2012, per a Dignity Memorial index; Timenote gives d. 01.04.2012). 'Lovingly remembered by Andris Lauris and his family': relationship not stated, a living third party. The obituary does not name her parents, but Timenote names her father Dāvis and maiden name Sirlaka, and gives her burial at Jaunrauna cemetery (ashes presumably returned to Latvia). She was a Red Cross-trained nurse: there is a 1955 file 'Grislis, Velta (Nee Sirlaks)' in the International Council of Nurses Nurse Refugee Files at the University of Pennsylvania, and Sirlaks hits in the Latvian Red Cross nurses' journal (Žēlsirdīgā Māsa, 1939–40). Her full name was Velta Skaidrīte.
cites.why: The birth year 1918, the 'late Janis' and Ontario all match the 1955 Hamilton marriage and Timenote.

cites.title: Changes of Names and Adoptions
cites.repository: HathiTrust (Univ. of California copy)
cites.note: No Oregon court adoption of Estella is published. The 'Changes of Names and Adoptions' lists printed in the Oregon Laws were read for 1914–1916 (1917 volume) and 1917–1918 (1919 volume). They contain no Alderson as adopter and no 'Phillis', 'Barns' or 'Estella' as a former name. By law, county judges reported every adoption to the Secretary of State for these lists through 1918.
cites.why: These are full, alphabetical, county-by-county lists, and the Alderson slot (between Adams and Allenback in 1917, Adams and Alkire in 1916) is empty. Caveats: the scan is OCR text, some courts reported late or not at all, and an adoption in 1919 or later would fall in the post-1920 ODHS era.

cites.title: About the Schubachs
cites.repository: Devar Emet Messianic Jewish Outreach, Skokie, Illinois
cites.quote: Over more than a decade, he translated every Hebrew and Aramaic verse of the Tanakh (Old Testament) three times, typically analyzing 22 verses a day. In this way, Wolf developed his own hyper-literal translation…
cites.note: His life's second work: a hyper-literal translation of the Hebrew Bible. "Wolf's love of Scripture led him to translating the Hebrew Bible into its most primitive roots in order to 'better understand God's message.' He nearly completed four passes from Genesis through Malachi by the end of 2018." Devar Emet, which holds his library, describes the method: "Over more than a decade, he translated every Hebrew and Aramaic verse of the Tanakh (Old Testament) three times, typically analyzing 22 verses a day… through the painstaking identification and expression of the unique meaning of each Hebrew word from its tripartite roots." He took courses at the Hebrew University in Jerusalem, supported field archaeologists, and attended biblical, archaeological and prophecy conferences.
cites.why: The obituary and the ministry that received the library describe the same work independently.

cites.quote: KERBRAT, YVES, also known as YVES J KERBRAT, was born 13 October 1924, was assigned Social Security number 559-18-4795 (indicating California), and died 16 February 1986, while residing in Zip Code 91342-0000. The Social Security field office at VAN NUYS CA received the claim 29 November 1975.
cites.note: Born 13 October 1924. Social Security number 559-18-4795, issued in California. He had no dates at all in the tree.
cites.why: Three Social Security–derived records (the Death Master File, the SSA application/claims file and the veterans' index) all give 13 October 1924 for a Yves J Kerbrat with one SSN, in California, where his daughter married in Los Angeles. The forename is rare — there is only one Yves Kerbrat in the whole index — but no record ties him explicitly to Jeanne, so this is a strong inference, not a proof.

cites.note: Inferred to have lived at age 1 with his parents François (Frank) Kerbrat and Ozanna Lheureux in Roseville, Macomb County, Michigan when his younger brother Adrien F. Kerbrat was born there on 27 April 1926 (eighteen months after Yves's 13 October 1924 birth).

cites.title: KERBRAT, YVES J & KERBRAT, FRANK (California SSN & Santa Monica field office)
cites.repository: sortedbyname.com (republication of the SSA NUMIDENT public file)
cites.quote: KERBRAT, YVES, also known as YVES J KERBRAT, was born 13 October 1924, was assigned Social Security number 559-18-4795 (indicating California), and died 16 February 1986, while residing in Zip Code 91342-0000. … KERBRAT, FRANK … The Social Security field office at SANTA MONICA CALIF received the claim 22 July 1952.
cites.note: Moved with his parents and brother Adrien from Michigan to California (where his parents filed Social Security claims at the Santa Monica field office in 1952 and 1956), and he and Adrien were issued sequential California Social Security numbers (559-18-4795 and 559-18-4798) prior to his 1950–1952 Korean War US Army service.
cites.why: His SSN prefix 559 attests California issuance before his 15 October 1950 US Army entry; his parents' 1952 and 1956 claims were filed at the Santa Monica field office.

cites.title: Rīga St Martin Latvian marriages 1911, no. 34 (summary list; main register no. 62)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 66, image 105 (left page, fol. 98v)
cites.quote: Бракомъ сочетавшіеся въ 1911 году. | 34 | Апрѣля двадцать второго | Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Зирлакъ сынъ Петра (Martin Wilhelm Sirlak) / Эрна Смукулъ, дочь Дава (Erna Smukul) | 62
cites.translation: Married in 1911. No. 34, 22 April: Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; Erna [Emma] Smukul, daughter of Dāvis. Main register no. 62.
cites.note: Married 22 Apr 1911 Julian (= 5 May 1911 Gregorian). Groom Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; bride written 'Erna' (Эрна / Erna) Smukul, daughter of Dāvis (Дава). The register here is only the year's summary list (no., date, names, fathers, and a reference to no. 62 of the main register, which is not in this volume), so no ages, residence, witnesses or banns. 'Erna' is taken as a clerk's slip for Emma: same clerk writes 'Эмма' plainly at no. 27. Confirms Emma's father's name Dāvis (her US SS record: Dāvis Smukuls) and places the marriage eight months before Elvīra's birth, in the same congregation that baptised her. Corrects the memoir's 'married young': he was 27, she 26.
cites.why: Groom's full double name and patronymic match his 1883 baptism; bride's surname and father Dāvis match Emma's SS record; same congregation as Elvīra's 1912 baptism. Only the bride's given name differs (Erna vs Emma). Verified by the parent on the crop.

cites.translation: 1875, March [page]. Born the 22nd [of February], 8:15[?] p.m.; baptised the same day as the entries above (9 March). No. 71. cites.note: Born [February] 22nd 1875 at 8¼[?] p.m.; baptised 9 March 1875 in the church by the parish pastor (Pastor loci). Parents: farm owner[?] ('Landesbesitzer'[?]) Peter Sirlak and Marrie née Gibboy, both Lutheran. Godparents: Md.[?] Kristine Gibboy (presumably a Gibbo relative of the mother), farmer (Wirth) Dahw Bitte and [his wife] Katrihne. Rauna Latvian baptisms 1875, no. 71. The birth month is not written on this line; it is carried down from no. 66 ('Februar'). Probably the eldest child, born a year after the Feb 1874 marriage. She is not in the 2015 tree. cites.quote: 1911 Декабря двадцать седьмого (27) 7 ч. веч. | 1912 Февраля девятнадцатаго (19) | № 82 | Эльвира Антонія (Elvira Antonie). Род. торговецъ Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Сирлакъ (Sirlak) ев. лют. вѣр. и его жена Эмма, ур. Смукулъ ев. лют. вѣроиспов. Воспр.: Давидъ Сирлакъ, хозяинъ; Анна Смукулъ, дѣв.; Эрнестина Сирлакъ, дѣвица. Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]
cites.translation: Born 27 December 1911, 7 p.m.; baptised 19 February 1912. No. 82. Elvira Antonie. Parents: trader Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Lutheran, and his wife Emma née Smukul, Ev.-Lutheran. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. Baptised [in …] by Pastor Hilde[?].
cites.note: Born 27 Dec 1911 Julian (= 9 Jan 1912 Gregorian) at 7 p.m.; baptised 19 Feb 1912 Julian (= 3 Mar 1912 Gregorian). Full baptismal name Elvira Antonie. Father: trader (торговецъ) Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, Ev.-Luth.; mother: his wife Emma née Smukul (the ending '-улъ' written over a struck-out ending), Ev.-Luth. Godparents: David Sirlak, farm owner (хозяинъ) [= her uncle Dāvis]; Anna Smukul, unmarried; Ernestine Sirlak, unmarried. The last line, in another hand, reads roughly 'Крещ. въ зал[ѣ][?] Ви[к]лес[ъ][?] паст. Гильде[?]' — baptised [at …] by Pastor Hilde[?]; place uncertain. Entry no. 82 sits among March baptisms, i.e. it was registered late, which is why date-ordered searches missed it. No residence is given (so Torņakalns is not confirmed here).
cites.why: Birth date to the hour matches the memoir's 9 Jan 1912 (= 27 Dec 1911 Julian); father's double name Martin Wilhelm and mother Emma née Smukul match; godparents are a Sirlaks farm owner David (her uncle Dāvis of Vīstuči) and a Smukul.

cites.title: Obituary: Vera Augenbergs, Indiana funeral home notices and obituaries (Indianapolis, Indiana), 7 December 2008
cites.repository: GenealogyBank
cites.quote: Vera Augenbergs 98, of Indianapolis, passed away December 7, 2008, a native of Ergli, Latvia, born July 3, 1910. She worked for Methodist Hospital for many years retiring in 1975 and was a member of Latvian Retiree s Association. Survivors include son, John Augenbergs of Farmingham, MI; two granddaughters, Inga and her husband, Dr. David Zadvinskis and Ivete and her husband, Ezequiel Larroquette; two great- grandsons, Lukas and Nahuel Larroquette. Service: Saturday December 13, 2008 1:00 p.m. at Flanner and Buchanan Funeral Center-Broad Ripple, with calling two hours prior. In lieu of flowers memorial contributions can be made to Latvian Evangelical Lutheran Church of Indianapolis 801 W. 73rd Street Indianapolis, Indiana 46260.
cites.note: father: Uģis Augenbergs
cites.why: The 7 Dec 2008 obituary of paternal grandmother Vera Augenbergs names her only child 'son, John [Jānis Uģis] Augenbergs of Farmingham, MI; two granddaughters, Inga and her husband, Dr. David Zadvinskis and Ivete and her husband, Ezequiel Larroquette; two great- grandsons, Lukas and Nahuel Larroquette'.
cites.as_recorded: Ivete and her husband, Ezequiel Larroquette (granddaughter of Vera Augenbergs; survivor alongside Vera's only child, son John [Uģis] Augenbergs)

The family says she was adopted. Every FamilySearch ancestor of Peter beyond generation 5, about 1,300 people back to the 1200s (Alderson, Royal, Newman, Brate, Cheesman, Stringham, Halsted, Schaeffer, English and Swedish gentry), therefore runs through her ADOPTIVE parents. Peter's biological lines on FamilySearch end at generation 3 (Danenbergs/Sirlaka) and generation 5 (Peter Hall, Peter McCabe: names only).

cites.title: Estella - Newman - Alderson - Et Al.
cites.repository: Washington State Archives, Digital Archives
cites.quote: Estella May Alderson ... Female ... May 5, 1916 ... Seattle ... King ... Winter Scott Alderson ... Carrie May Newman ... * Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated. ** Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth. ... I certify that no prior certificate has been found for this registrant ... Filed at Seattle, Washington, on April 7, 1952
cites.note: Delayed certificate filed 7 Apr 1952 (Vol. 26, State File No. 342). It names Winter Scott Alderson (b. Oregon, age 50) and Carrie May Newman (b. New York, age 38) as parents. Supporting evidence: (1) affidavit of Carrie May Schroeder, 18 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated'; (2) affidavit of Mrs. Lola Webster, 25 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth'; (3) Portland Public Schools transcript, 1922–1923 ('Scott Alderson', 'May Alderson'). Registrar's certification: 'no prior certificate has been found for this registrant'. Signed by Estella May Hall, sworn at Portland, 13 Mar 1952.
cites.why: Primary document for date and place. It agrees with every census (b. Washington) and with the SSDI (5 May 1916). The parentage in it rests on the adoptive family's own affidavits, and the registrar found no original certificate under the Alderson name. That is what an original filed under another name would produce.

cites.title: Changes of Names and Adoptions
cites.repository: HathiTrust (Univ. of California copy)
cites.note: No Oregon court adoption of Estella is published. The 'Changes of Names and Adoptions' lists printed in the Oregon Laws were read for 1914–1916 (1917 volume) and 1917–1918 (1919 volume). They contain no Alderson as adopter and no 'Phillis', 'Barns' or 'Estella' as a former name. By law, county judges reported every adoption to the Secretary of State for these lists through 1918.
cites.why: These are full, alphabetical, county-by-county lists, and the Alderson slot (between Adams and Allenback in 1917, Adams and Alkire in 1916) is empty. Caveats: the scan is OCR text, some courts reported late or not at all, and an adoption in 1919 or later would fall in the post-1920 ODHS era.

cites.title: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) soul revision 1834, XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family 4 (Sillak)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: [XXIX. Leis-Sparing] / ... / 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben | — / deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof | — / " 2 " Marz | nachher geb. | — | 12. / " 3 " Jahn | nachher geb. | — | 4. ‖ 4. | Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.
cites.translation: [XXIX. Lejas-Spāriņi]: ... Family 4: Sillak Jahn, Ansche's son, manor weaver, from the manor people, died in 1830; his 1st son Dawe, ditto, 1829 to Lindenhof [Liepa] estate; 2nd son Marz, born since, 12; 3rd son Jahn, born since, 4. Sillak Masche, Ansche's daughter, his wife, 59.
cites.note: Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) 8th soul revision (1834, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 112), farm XXIX. Leis-Sparing, family no. 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | v. d. Hofsleuten | 1830 gestorben' (manor weaver, came from the manor people, where in the 1826 surname revision on image 58 he was listed as 'IV. Sirlack | Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber | 1825 v. Gute Wesselshof zugekommen | 47'; died in 1830); his 1st son Dawe ('deßen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof' — moved in 1829 to Liepa / Lindenhof manor, where he later appears as churchwarden 'Kirchenvorm. Dahwis Sillak' in 1859–62); his 2nd son Marz ('2 Sohn Marz | nachher geb. | 12', born c. 1822 — our ancestor Mārcis Sirlaks, who moved from No. XXIX Leis-Sparing to No. XIV Wihstuz and fathered Pēteris Sirlaks in 1847); his 3rd son Jahn ('3 Sohn Jahn | nachher geb. | 4', born c. 1830 — who also moved from No. XXIX to No. XIV Wihstuz by 1850, age 20); and his widow 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau | 59.' (matching her age 51 in 1826 + 8 = 59).
cites.why: Proves that Mārcis Sirlaks (b. c. 1822, father of Pēteris Sirlaks 1847–1896 at XIV. Wihstuz, recorded in 1850 as 'Marz Sillak, Jahns Sohn, aus No. XXIX') is the 2nd son of 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn' (who came to Jaunrauna from Wesselshof / Veselauska in 1825 and died in 1830 at XXIX. Leis-Sparing) × 'Masche, Ansche Tochter', and NOT the son of the other 'IV. Sirlack' head of household 'Jahn, Martz Sohn, Hofsknecht' (who died in 1821 leaving only son Peter b. c. 1814).
cites.as_recorded: 4. | Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber (1830 gestorben); deßen 1 Sohn Dawe; 2 Sohn Marz; 3 Sohn Jahn; Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, deßen Frau

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1834, farm XXIX Leis Sparing, family 4
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 4. Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber[?] | aus Hofsleute[?] | 1830[?] gestorben / dessen 1 Sohn Dawe | dito | 1829 nach dem Gute Lindenhof[?] / " 2 " Marz | nachhergeboren | | 12. / " 3 " Jahn | nachgeboren | | 4. — Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, dessen Frau | 59.
cites.translation: Jahn Sillak, son of Ansis, manor weaver, from the manor people, died 1830; his 1st son Dāvis, moved 1829 to Lindenhof estate; 2nd son Mārcis, born since the last revision, 12; 3rd son Jānis, born since, 4. Masche Sillak, daughter of Ansis, his wife, 59.
cites.note: 1834 revision (8th), farm XXIX Leis Sparing, family 4: 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber[?]' — died 1830[?] (digit overwritten; possibly 1828); his 1st son Dawe, moved 1829 to the estate Lindenhof[?]; 2nd son Marz, born after 1816, 12 (b. c. 1822); 3rd son Jahn, born after 1816, 4. Female side: 'Sillak Masche, Ansche Tochter, dessen Frau', 59. Earliest appearance of the surname (as Sillak); Mārcis was the son of Jahn and Masche.
cites.why: Name, father Jahn, brother Jahn (20 in 1850 under the same family), farm XXIX matching the 1850 'aus No. XXIX', and age 12 → 28 all agree. Read by a sub-agent; not re-read by the parent. Masche's age (59, so c. 47 at Mārcis's birth) is doubtful.

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1816, manor people
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31 (fol. 26); farm 29 on image 54 (fol. 49)
cites.quote: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29 | 32. | 37. / Sohn Dawe, nachhergeboren | ½ — Jahns Eheweib Masche, Ansch T. 41
cites.translation: Weaver Jahn, son of Ansis, from no. 29, 32 [in 1811], 37 [now]; son Dāvis, born since, ½. Jahn's wife Masche, daughter of Ansis, 41.
cites.note: 1816 revision (7th), manor people: weaver Jahn, son of Ansch (Ansis), from farm no. 29, aged 32 in 1811 and 37 in 1816 (b. c. 1779); son Dawe, born after 1811, ½. Wife Masche, daughter of Ansch, 41 (b. c. 1775); daughters Trine 16, Anne 14, Marri 10, Liese 5. No surname yet (surnames were assigned in Livonia c. 1822–1826). Also on farm 29 (image 54): farmhand Jahn son of Ansch 'in B', son Peter d. 1814; and young Jahn son of Ansch 'in No. 20'. Died 1830[?] per the 1834 list.
cites.why: Identification with the 1834 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' rests on the same name and patronymic, a wife Masche daughter of Ansch in both lists (41 → 59, exactly +18 years), son Dawe born after 1811, the trade (weaver) and origin farm 29. Without a surname, a second Jahn son of Ansch on the same estate leaves some doubt.
cites.as_recorded: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29

(matching her age 51 in 1826 + 8 = 59).
cites.why: Proves that Mārcis Sirlaks (b. c. 1822, father of Pēteris Sirlaks 1847–1896 at XIV. Wihstuz, recorded in 1850 as 'Marz Sillak, Jahns Sohn, aus No. XXIX') is the 2nd son of 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn' (who came to Jaunrauna from Wesselshof / Veselauska in 1825 and died in 1830 at XXIX. Leis-Sparing) × 'Masche, Ansche Tochter', and NOT the son of the other 'IV. Sirlack' head of household 'Jahn, Martz Sohn, Hofsknecht' (who died in 1821 leaving only son Peter b. c. 1814).

cites.translation: Farm No. XIV Vīstuči … family 15/95: Mārcis Sirlaks, son of Jānis, aged 28 at the last revision, 36 now; his stepson[?] Dāvis Vīstucs, 14; son Pēteris Sirlaks, 10. His wife Anne, widow of [a] Vīstucs, 51.
cites.note: 1858 revision list (10th revision), family no. 95 (9th revision no. 15). Marz Sillakk, son of Jahn: aged 28 at the 1850 revision, 36 now (so b. c. 1821/22). His stepson[?] Dahw Wihstuz: 6 → 14. Son Peter Sillakk: 2 → 10. Female side: 'his wife Anne, widowed Wihstuz', 51 (so b. c. 1806/07). So Anne was the widow of a Wihstuz (the farm's earlier family) and Dahw Wihstuz is Peter's older half-brother. Gives Pēteris's grandfather's name, Jānis (Jahn), and the patronymic of Mārcis.
cites.why: Peter, son of Marz, aged 10 at the Vīstuči farm matches the 1847 baptism of Peter, son of Mahrz Sirlakk and Anne, at Wihstuz. 'Sillakk' is the revision clerk's spelling; the family index of the same volume lists it as 'Sillak' (no. 95).

cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti

cites.quote: [August] — sechsten Morg. 8 Uhr | — sechzehnten | 149. Freudenberg K. Pohdis. Marie Gibboij. Lett. Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. W. Anne, luth. T. Lej Pohdis Jehkabs Pohdis u. s. W. Lihse, K. Pohdis Marie Bitte.
cites.translation: Born [August] the sixth, 8 a.m.; baptised the sixteenth. No. 149. Freudenberg, Upper Pohdis farm. Marie Gibboy. [Parents:] Latvian farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutheran. Godparents: from Lower Pohdis, Jēkabs Pohdis and his wife Līze; from Upper Pohdis, Marie Bitte.
cites.note: Born 6 Aug 1853 Julian (= 18 Aug 1853 Gregorian) at 8 a.m.; baptised 16 Aug 1853. Daughter of Latvian farmhand (Kn. = Knecht) Mahrzis (Mārcis) Gibboy and his wife Anne, Lutherans (mother by given name only, as usual in 1853). Godparents: Jehkabs Pohdis and his wife Lihse of Lejas-Pohdis, and Marie Bitte[?] of Kalna-Pohdis. The 71st legitimate girl of the year. The same volume shows a farm named 'Gibboy' on Freudenberg (marriages 1853 no. 21), the likely origin of the surname, and the death of an unmarried maidservant Masche Gibboy, aged 58⅔, at Freudenberg Lejas-Dauksche (deaths 1853 no. 154). Kristīne Gibboy, Marie's probable sister and godmother of Mārtiņš Sirlaks in 1883, should be among later Freudenberg births (Cēsis rural Dz 1847–1879, LVVA 235/7/104).
cites.why: Given name, surname (the same 'Gibboy' spelling as her 1874 marriage and her children's baptisms), exact date of the relative's tree (6 Aug 1853, so the tree uses the Julian date) and the tree's place 'Priekuļi' (= Freudenberg) all match. Verified on the crop. Not formally linked to the 1874 bride by a stated age or parents, so 'high' rests on the coincidence of all four details.

cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: [Dec.] einunddreißigste Morg 7 Uhr | [Januar] sechste z. H. get. | 214. Freudenberg K. Pohding Kristine Gibboij El: Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. Wb. Anne, luth Tf. W. Gibboij Jahnis Sarriht u. Dahwis Sarriht. W. Gibboij M. Marie Sarriht

cites.note: Cēsis rural Lutheran birth register 1855, entry no. 214 (legitimate female no. 106): Kristine Gibboij, born 31 December 1855 O.S. at 7 a.m. (= 12 January 1856 N.S.) at Freudenberg Kalna-Podiņi ('Freudenberg K. Pohding'), baptised at home ('z. H. get.') on 6 January 1856 O.S. (= 18 January 1856 N.S.). Parents: farmhand Mahrzis Gibboij and his wife Anne, Lutheran ('El: Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij u. s. Wb. Anne, luth'). Godparents: Jahnis Sarriht and Dahwis Sarriht of Vec-Ģiboli, and maid Marie Sarriht of Vec-Ģiboli ('Tf. W. Gibboij Jahnis Sarriht u. Dahwis Sarriht. W. Gibboij M. Marie Sarriht'). Because she was born on the very last day of 1855 Old Style (12 January 1856 New Style) and baptised in January 1856, she matches both '2. Kristine, 2' in the November 1857 Priekuļi soul revision of Mārcis Ģibols (age 50) × Anne (age 38) at Rauguļi AND the Kristīne Ģibola (b. c. 1856) who married Jānis Kārnītis in Rauna on 20 June 1882 at age 26.
cites.why: Resolves Kristīne Ģibola's primary birth record and explains why the 1857 revision gives her age as 2 (born end of 1855 O.S.) while her 1882 marriage entry gives her age as 26 (born Jan 1856 N.S. / baptised Jan 1856 O.S.).

cites.title: Rauna births 1886 no. 33
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, img 311 (right page)
cites.quote: 1885 December fünf u. zwanzig[sten] abends 9 U. | zweiten | 33 Lubar, Lj. Luhzmann[?] / Emma Smukkul / Elt. Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. d. Marie geb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch / Tf. Md. Juhle Meeschit[?], Md. Leene Leepin[?], Jg. August Meeschit[?]
cites.translation: 1885 December twenty-fifth, 9 in the evening | [baptised on the] second | No. 33, Lubar[?], [farm] Luhzmann[?] / Emma Smukkul / parents: farmhand (Knecht) Dahw Smukkul and his wife Marie née Kahjon, both Lutheran / godparents: maid Juhle Meeschit[?], maid Leene Leepin[?], young man August Meeschit[?]
cites.note: Born 25 Dec 1885 (Julian), 9 p.m. = 6 Jan 1886 (Gregorian). Baptised 2 Feb 1886 (Julian) = 14 Feb 1886 (Gregorian): the baptism column has 'zweiten' directly beneath entry no. 32's 'Februar zweiten' (img/sf-rauna-1886-dz31-33-dates.jpg). Entry is in the 1886 register.
cites.why: Child's name, both parents (Dahw Smukkul + Marie geb. Kahjon = DP card 'Dāvis Smukuls, Marija Kajans[?]') and day/month (6 Jan Gregorian) all match the Arolsen DP card. The DP card's year 1885 is the Julian birth year. The 1947 '6.6.85 Branti' reading is therefore wrong or garbled; Branti is not named here.

cites.title: Rīga St Martin Latvian marriages 1911, no. 34 (summary list; main register no. 62)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 3036, apr. 4, l. 66, image 105 (left page, fol. 98v)
cites.quote: Бракомъ сочетавшіеся въ 1911 году. | 34 | Апрѣля двадцать второго | Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Зирлакъ сынъ Петра (Martin Wilhelm Sirlak) / Эрна Смукулъ, дочь Дава (Erna Smukul) | 62
cites.translation: Married in 1911. No. 34, 22 April: Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; Erna [Emma] Smukul, daughter of Dāvis. Main register no. 62.
cites.note: Married 22 Apr 1911 Julian (= 5 May 1911 Gregorian). Groom Martin Wilhelm Sirlak, son of Pēteris; bride written 'Erna' (Эрна / Erna) Smukul, daughter of Dāvis (Дава). The register here is only the year's summary list (no., date, names, fathers, and a reference to no. 62 of the main register, which is not in this volume), so no ages, residence, witnesses or banns. 'Erna' is taken as a clerk's slip for Emma: same clerk writes 'Эмма' plainly at no. 27. Confirms Emma's father's name Dāvis (her US SS record: Dāvis Smukuls) and places the marriage eight months before Elvīra's birth, in the same congregation that baptised her. Corrects the memoir's 'married young': he was 27, she 26.
cites.why: Groom's full double name and patronymic match his 1883 baptism; bride's surname and father Dāvis match Emma's SS record; same congregation as Elvīra's 1912 baptism. Only the bride's given name differs (Erna vs Emma). Verified by the parent on the crop.
cites.as_recorded: Мартинъ Вильгельмъ Зирлакъ сынъ Петра (Martin Wilhelm Sirlak) / Эрна Смукулъ дочь Дава (Erna Smukul)

cites.title: Rauna births 1889 no. 243
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, img 432 (right page)
cites.quote: September, dritten, morgens 2 U. | achten. | 243. Ronneburg, Lappul. Anna Smukkul. Elt. Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch. Pth. Mch. Karline Kahjon, Jg. Jahn Kahjon, W. Mari Meesiht. Get. v. Pastor Dsirne in der Kirche.
cites.translation: Born 3 September, 2 a.m.; baptised 8th. No. 243. Rauna, Lapuļi. Anna Smukkul. Parents: farmhand Dāvis Smukkul and wife Mari née Kahjon, both Lutheran. Godparents: maiden Karlīne Kahjon, bachelor Jānis Kahjon, wife Mari Meesiht. Baptised by Pastor Dsirne in the church.
cites.note: Born 3 Sep 1889 at 2 a.m. (Julian; 15 Sep 1889 Gregorian), baptised 8 Sep 1889 by Pastor Dsirne in the church. Legitimate daughter of 'Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon, beide lutherisch' (farmhand Dāvis Smukulis and wife Marija née Kajons, married 28 Oct 1884 in Rauna, 1884 no. 42). Godparents: 'Mch. Karline Kahjon, Jg. Jahn Kahjon, W. Mari Meesiht'. Younger full biological sister of Emma Smukkul (b. 25 Dec 1885 Jul. = 6 Jan 1886 Greg. at Lubar, Lj: Luhzmann, 1886 no. 33, to the same parents 'Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Marie geb. Kahjon', with Meesiht godparents 'Md. Juhle Meesiht' and 'Jg. August Meesiht'); by Sep 1889 the family had moved from Lubāra (Lūcmaņi) to Rauna manor's Lapuļi farm (where Wth. Peter Kahjon × Anna geb. Mise also lived in 1886–1890). Crucially, at the baptism of Emma Smukule and Mārtiņš Vilhelms Sirlaks's daughter Elvīra Antonija Sirlaka on 19 Feb 1912 (Rīga St Martin 1912 no. 82), the godmother from the mother's side was 'Anna Smukul' — Emma's younger full sister Anna (b. Sep 1889, age 22 in Feb 1912).
cites.why: Parents' names and mother's maiden name ('Kn. Dahw Smukkul u. W. Mari gb. Kahjon') are identical to 1884 marriage no. 42 and Emma Smukkul's 1886 birth no. 33, both sisters share Meesiht godparents, and Anna is the exact match for the 1912 godmother Anna Smukul.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 58 | — | 68 / XIV Meschzeem | Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn | 30 | — | 40 / Marz des Jahns 1te Sohn | 6 | — | 16 / Jahn ,, 2te Sohn | 2½ | — | 12½ ‖ XIV Meschzeem | Masche deßen Weib | 50 / XIV Meschzeem | Liese deßen Weib | 40 / Mareet ihre 1te Tochter | 14½ / Anne ihre 2te Tochter | 4
cites.translation: Surname XIV Meschzeem: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 58 -> 68; his wife Masche, 50. Jahn, Jacob's 1st son, 30 -> 40; his wife Liese, 40; Jahn's 1st son Marz, 6 -> 16; 2nd son Jahn, 2½ -> 12½; their 1st daughter Mareet, 14½; their 2nd daughter Anne, 4.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 1826 surname revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 54, ff. 49v–50r), farm 1. Meschzeem, surname No. XIV Meschzeem (second farmer's household): farmer Jacob, Jahn's son ('Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, now 68 (b. c. 1758), and his wife Masche, age 50 (b. c. 1776); Jacob's 1st son Jahn ('Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn'), age 30 in 1816, now 40 (b. c. 1786), and his wife Liese, age 40 (b. c. 1786); their sons 1. Marz (6 -> 16) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 12½); their daughters 1. Mareet (14½) and 2. Anne ('Anne ihre 2te Tochter'), age 4 in 1826 (born c. 1822). Also listed are Jacob's 2nd son Dawe (16 in 1816, 's. in No 10'), 4th son Jacob (2½ -> 12½), daughters Juhle (17) and Masche (15), and farmer's brother Peter, Jahn's son ('Peter, Jahns Sohn Wirthsbruder', 47 -> 57; wife Anne, 41).
cites.why: Identifies Anne Meschzeem at age 4 in the 1826 surname revision with her parents Jānis Mežciems (40) × Līze (40), paternal grandparents Jēkabs Jāņa d. Mežciems (68) × Maža (50), and paternal great-grandfather Jānis (Jahn).
cites.as_recorded: XIV Meschzeem | Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth; Masche deßen Weib; Jahn des Jacobs 1te Sohn; Liese deßen Weib; Anne ihre 2te Tochter

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1834, I. Meschzeem, family 1
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 1. | Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth | 58 | 1832 gestorben | — / dessen Sohn 1 Jahn | 29 | 1833 gestorben | — / dessen Söhne 1 Marz | 6 | — | 24 / 2 Jahn | 2½ | — | 20½ / 2 Dawe | 16 | vide N XXVIII | — / 3 Jakob jetziger Wirth | 2½ | — | 20½ ‖ 1 | dessen Wittwe Masche | 57 / dessen Wittwe Lihse | 47 / dessen Frau Babbe | 22 / dessen Töchter 1 Mareet | 21½ / 2 Anne | 11
cites.translation: Family 1: Jakob Meschzeem, former farmer, 58 [in 1816], died in 1832; his widow Masche, 57. His 1st son Jahn, 29 [in 1816], died in 1833; his widow Lihse, 47. His [Jahn's] sons: 1. Marz, 6 -> 24 (his wife Babbe, 22); 2. Jahn, 2½ -> 20½; his [Jahn's] daughters: 1. Mareet, 21½; 2. Anne, 11. [Jakob Sr.'s sons:] 2. Dawe, 16, see No. XXVIII; 3. Jakob, current farmer, 2½ -> 20½.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 8th soul revision, dated 31 March 1834 O.S. (= 12 April 1834 N.S., LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 117, ff. 115v–116r), farm I. Meschzeem, family no. 1: former farmer Jakob Meschzeem ('Jakob Meschzeem ehemals Wirth'), age 58 in 1816, died in 1832 ('1832 gestorben'), leaving widow Masche, age 57; his 1st son Jahn ('dessen Sohn 1 Jahn'), age 29 in 1816, died in 1833 ('1833 gestorben'), leaving widow Lihse, age 47; Jahn's sons 1. Marz (6 -> 24; wife Babbe, 22) and 2. Jahn (2½ -> 20½); Jahn's daughters 1. Mareet (21½) and 2. Anne (11, born c. 1822/23). Jakob's 3rd son Jakob (2½ -> 20½) is now the current farmer ('3 Jakob jetziger Wirth').
cites.why: Records the exact death years of Anne Meschzeem's grandfather Jēkabs Mežciems (died 1832) and father Jānis Mežciems (died 1833), and shows 11-year-old Anne Meschzeem with her widowed mother Līze (47) and grandmother Maža (57) at I. Meschzeem.

cites.title: Jaunrauna estate revision 1816, manor people
cites.repository: LVVA, via Raduraksti
cites.locator: LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31 (fol. 26); farm 29 on image 54 (fol. 49)
cites.quote: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29 | 32. | 37. / Sohn Dawe, nachhergeboren | ½ — Jahns Eheweib Masche, Ansch T. 41
cites.translation: Weaver Jahn, son of Ansis, from no. 29, 32 [in 1811], 37 [now]; son Dāvis, born since, ½. Jahn's wife Masche, daughter of Ansis, 41.
cites.note: 1816 revision (7th), manor people: weaver Jahn, son of Ansch (Ansis), from farm no. 29, aged 32 in 1811 and 37 in 1816 (b. c. 1779); son Dawe, born after 1811, ½. Wife Masche, daughter of Ansch, 41 (b. c. 1775); daughters Trine 16, Anne 14, Marri 10, Liese 5. No surname yet (surnames were assigned in Livonia c. 1822–1826). Also on farm 29 (image 54): farmhand Jahn son of Ansch 'in B', son Peter d. 1814; and young Jahn son of Ansch 'in No. 20'. Died 1830[?] per the 1834 list.
cites.why: Identification with the 1834 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' rests on the same name and patronymic, a wife Masche daughter of Ansch in both lists (41 → 59, exactly +18 years), son Dawe born after 1811, the trade (weaver) and origin farm 29. Without a surname, a second Jahn son of Ansch on the same estate leaves some doubt.
cites.as_recorded: Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1811, No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 6 Gibboy Gesinde / Ansche 1ster Wirth | 53 | gestorben im Jahr 1805 | — / deßen Söhne 1, Martz Wirth | 20 | — | 36 / ... / Laur | 46 | — | 62 / deßen Sohn Jahn | 6 | — | 22 / Peter | 30 | — | 46 / deßen Sohn Martz | — | nachher gebohren | 5
cites.translation: No. 6 Gibboy farm: Ansche, 1st farmer, 53 [in 1795], died in 1805; his sons: 1. Martz, farmer, 20 -> 36 ... Laur, 46 -> 62; his son Jahn, 6 -> 22; Peter, 30 [in 1795] -> 46 [in 1811]; his son Martz, born since, 5 [in 1811].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 6th soul revision (dated August 1811, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 9, p. 3v), farm No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde: in the first household (headed by 1st farmer Ansche, 53 in 1795, died 1805, and his son Martz Wirth, 20 -> 36, with Laur, 46 -> 62, and Laur's son Jahn, 6 -> 22) is listed farmhand Peter, age 30 in 1795, now age 46 in 1811 (born c. 1765), and his son Martz ('deßen Sohn Martz'), born after 1795 ('nachher gebohren'), age 5 in 1811 (born c. 1806).
cites.why: Earliest revision record of Mārcis Ģibols (1806/07–1882, father of Marija Ģibola) at age 5 with his father Pēteris (age 46, b. c. 1765) at the ancestral Gibboy (Ģiboli) farm.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1816, No. 21 Schwigur
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 21 Schwigur / Wirth Peter Jahn Sohn | 46 | — | 50 / ... / Knecht Martz Peters Sohn | 5 | — | 9
cites.translation: No. 21 Schwigur [Švīguļi]: Farmer Peter, Jahn's son, 46 -> 50 ... farmhand Martz, Peter's son, 5 [in 1811] -> 9 [in 1816].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 7th soul revision (1816, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 43, ff. 37v–38r), farm No. 21 Schwigur: at the bottom of the household of farmer Peter Jahn Sohn (46 -> 50) is 'Knecht Martz Peters Sohn', age 5 at the 1811 revision, now age 9 in 1816 (born c. 1806/07). In the 1826 surname revision at No. 21 Schwigur (image 75), this exact entry is assigned surname 'VII Gibboi' and cross-referenced to No. 16 Pohding ('VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn s. in No 16 | 9').
cites.why: Bridges the 5-year-old 'Martz, Peter's son' at No. 6 Gibboy in 1811 to 'Marz, Peters Sohn [VII Gibboi]' at No. 21 Schwigur -> No. 16 Pohding in 1826.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) surname revision 1826, No. 1 Meschzeem (surname XIV Meschzeem)
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: 16. Pohding / Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth | 29 | 1825 gestorben | — ‖ XXXI Pohdin | Marri deßen Wittwe s. unten verheirathet an Marz Gibboi / ... / VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21 | — | 19 ‖ VII Gibboi | Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob | 35
cites.translation: No. 16 Pohding [Podiņi]: Jacob, Jahn's son, farmer, 29 [in 1816], died in 1825; [surname XXXI Pohdin] Marri, his widow, see below married to Marz Gibboi ... [surname VII Gibboi] Marz, Peter's son, farmer, from No. 21, 19; [surname VII Gibboi] Marri, his wife, see above widow of Jacob, 35.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 1826 surname revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 69, ff. 64v–65r), farm 16. Pohding: the previous farmer Jacob, Jahn's son ('Jacob Jahns Sohn Wirth', age 29 in 1816) died in 1825 ('1825 gestorben'), leaving son Laur (2¾ -> 12¾), daughters Triene (10¾), Anne (8), and Marri (6), and widow Marri ('XXXI Pohdin | Marri deßen Wittwe s. unten verheirathet an Marz Gibboi'). At the bottom of the same farm, 'VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21', age 19 in 1826 (born c. 1806/07), has come from No. 21 Schwigur, married Jacob's 35-year-old widow Marri ('VII Gibboi | Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob | 35'), and become the farmer (Wirth) of 16. Pohding.
cites.why: Explains how 19-year-old Mārcis Ģibols (son of Pēteris of Ģiboli, raised at Švīguļi) became farmer (Wirth) of No. 16 Podiņi in 1825/26 by marrying the 35-year-old widow Marri of Podiņi, and why he remarried in October 1847 to Anne Meschzeem after Marri's death.
cites.as_recorded: VII Gibboi | Marz, Peters Sohn Wirth aus No 21; Marri deßen Wb, sieh oben Wittwe des Jacob
