cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1857, XIX Gibboi farm, family 10/58
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde. | 10. | 58. | Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth | 34½. | 41½. / 2. Jahn Wirthsgehülfe[?] | 28. | 35. / dessen Sohn Marz | 1855 nachgeboren | 2. / 3. Dahw | 25½.
cites.translation: Farm XIX Ģiboļi. Family 10/58: Jahn's sons 1. Mārcis Gibboi, farmer, 34½ then, 41½ now; 2. Jānis, farmer's assistant[?], 28, 35; his son Mārcis, born 1855, 2; 3. Dāvis, 25½.
cites.note: The 1857 soul revision's column for the last revision (1850), XIX Gibboi farm, family 10: 'Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi' 34½, '2. Jahn' 28, '3. Dahw' 25½ (so b. c. 1816, 1822 and 1824/25): the sons of a Jahn, on this farm in 1850. Dahw has no age for 1857; the note beside him reads roughly 'by order of the Kameralhof of 18[?] … 1856, No. 652, transferred to Riga' [?]. The 1850 revision itself (f. 199/1/112) has not been read for this farm.
cites.why: Read at full size (Round 3). The three are the sons Mārcis (b. 1816), Jānis (b. 1822) and Dāvis (b. 1825) of Jānis Ģibols (1790–1847) × Masche in Raimonds's tree: the father's name and all three ages agree. The page names no mother.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1811, No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 6 Gibboy Gesinde / Ansche 1ster Wirth | 53 | gestorben im Jahr 1805 | — / deßen Söhne 1, Martz Wirth | 20 | — | 36 / ... / Laur | 46 | — | 62 / deßen Sohn Jahn | 6 | — | 22 / Peter | 30 | — | 46 / deßen Sohn Martz | — | nachher gebohren | 5
cites.translation: No. 6 Gibboy farm: Ansche, 1st farmer, 53 [in 1795], died in 1805; his sons: 1. Martz, farmer, 20 -> 36 ... Laur, 46 -> 62; his son Jahn, 6 -> 22; Peter, 30 [in 1795] -> 46 [in 1811]; his son Martz, born since, 5 [in 1811].
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 6th soul revision (dated August 1811, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 9, p. 3v), farm No. 6 Gibboy Gesinde: in the first household (headed by 1st farmer Ansche, 53 in 1795, died 1805, and his son Martz Wirth, 20 -> 36, with Laur, 46 -> 62, and Laur's son Jahn, 6 -> 22) is listed farmhand Peter, age 30 in 1795, now age 46 in 1811 (born c. 1765), and his son Martz ('deßen Sohn Martz'), born after 1795 ('nachher gebohren'), age 5 in 1811 (born c. 1806).
cites.why: Earliest revision record of Mārcis Ģibols (1806/07–1882, father of Marija Ģibola) at age 5 with his father Pēteris (age 46, b. c. 1765) at the ancestral Gibboy (Ģiboli) farm.

cites.title: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision 1816, No. 19 Gibbain
cites.repository: Latvian State Historical Archives (LVVA), via Raduraksti
cites.quote: No 19 Gibbain / Wirth Marting Ansche Sohn | 36 | — | 40 / Marteng Sohn Jacob | 6 | — | 10 / Knecht Laure Ansche Sohn | 62 | — | 66 / Laure Sohn Jahn | 22 | — | 26 / Jahn Sohn Martze | neugebohren | ¼ / Knecht Peter Ansche Sohn | 46 | gestorben | —
cites.translation: No. 19 Gibbain [Ģiboli]: Farmer Marting, Ansche's son, 36 -> 40; Marting's son Jacob, 6 -> 10; farmhand Laure, Ansche's son, 62 -> 66; Laure's son Jahn, 22 -> 26; Jahn's son Martze, newborn, ¼; farmhand Peter, Ansche's son, 46 [in 1811], died.
cites.note: Priekuļi (Freudenberg) 7th soul revision (1816, LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 41, ff. 35v–36r), farm No. 19 Gibbain (renumbered from No. 6 Gibboy in 1811): following farmer Marting Ansche Sohn (36 -> 40) and farmhand Laure Ansche Sohn (62 -> 66) is 'Knecht Peter Ansche Sohn', age 46 at the 1811 revision, now recorded as 'gestorben' (died between 1811 and 1816). This gives Pēteris's patronymic — Ansche Sohn (son of Ansis, like Laure Ansche Sohn b. c. 1749 and 1st farmer Ansche b. c. 1742) — and explains why his orphaned 9-year-old son Martz Peters Sohn (age 5 in 1811) appears two farms over at No. 21 Schwigur in 1816.
cites.why: Identifies the grandfather of Mārcis Ģibols (1806/07–1882) as Ansis (Ansche) and records the death of Mārcis's father Pēteris Ansis's son (b. c. 1765) between 1811 and 1816 at Ģiboli.

cites.title: Estella - Newman - Alderson - Et Al.
cites.repository: Washington State Archives, Digital Archives
cites.quote: Estella May Alderson ... Female ... May 5, 1916 ... Seattle ... King ... Winter Scott Alderson ... Carrie May Newman ... * Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated. ** Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth. ... I certify that no prior certificate has been found for this registrant ... Filed at Seattle, Washington, on April 7, 1952
cites.note: Delayed certificate filed 7 Apr 1952 (Vol. 26, State File No. 342). It names Winter Scott Alderson (b. Oregon, age 50) and Carrie May Newman (b. New York, age 38) as parents. Supporting evidence: (1) affidavit of Carrie May Schroeder, 18 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the mother of the child stated'; (2) affidavit of Mrs. Lola Webster, 25 Mar 1952, 'Affiant states she is the older sister of the child and lived in Seattle with her parents at the time of the birth'; (3) Portland Public Schools transcript, 1922–1923 ('Scott Alderson', 'May Alderson'). Registrar's certification: 'no prior certificate has been found for this registrant'. Signed by Estella May Hall, sworn at Portland, 13 Mar 1952.
cites.why: Primary document for date and place. It agrees with every census (b. Washington) and with the SSDI (5 May 1916). The parentage in it rests on the adoptive family's own affidavits, and the registrar found no original certificate under the Alderson name. That is what an original filed under another name would produce.

leads.title: Where and when Charles H. Hall Sr. married Susan McCabe
leads.question: Hall / McCabe (Peter's mother's father's side)
leads.claim: They married c. 1918, before Margaret Ellen's birth in Jan 1919, probably in Oregon, California or Washington.

evidence_for.note: Overlooked until 2026-10-25: Peter's own 2015 tree (S-legacy-2015, unions 44) gives the marriage date as 17 Aug 1917, with no place. On that day Charles was in El Portal, Mariposa Co., CA: his draft card (5 Jun 1917) says single, he was examined by the Mariposa board on 18 Aug, and he was inducted from Mariposa on 19 Sep. So if the date is right, the marriage was most likely in **California** (Mariposa, Merced or San Francisco), and Susan was in California in 1917. Where the 2015 tree got the date is unknown (ask Peter's mother).

Charles H. Hall Sr.: marriage 1910/1930 Washington State (all counties). NEGATIVE: no marriage of Charles Hall x Susan/Susie McCabe in the WA statewide marriage index 1910-1930. Searched by groom Hall/Charles (1914-25), bride McCabe (1910-30), groom Hall + bride Susie/Susan, and groom Hall + bride McCabe with Soundex. Clark Co. Charles Hall marriages 1920-21 are to Bagby, Nettie Hall, Poole and Webber, none ours.
evidence_for.quote: (search result lists; none matching)
evidence_for.why: The index is broad but not guaranteed complete. The marriage may have been in Oregon (Portland), in California, after 1930, or under variant names.

sources.title: Searches listed in README.md §1

evidence_against.note: Not in the Washington statewide marriage index 1910–1930 (searched by groom, by bride and with Soundex). Susan said 'married 1930' in one census, which may mean the marriage is later or the answer social.

2026-10-25: WA Digital Archives searched by hand, all counties 1910–1925, including Skamania (title 438, 1910s indexed): no Charles Hall × Susan McCabe, and no Susan McCabe marriage at all. Multnomah Co. OR: GFO's typed index of 54,264 marriages 1900–1924 (complete for 1916–19) has no Susan McCabe and no Charles Hall × Susan. Clean negatives.

leads.title: "Jewish ancestry, never tell anyone": a family story on the Danenberg side
leads.question: Family lore and other
leads.claim: There is Jewish ancestry on the Danenberg side.

evidence_for.note: Family lore, apocryphally from vecmama (Elvīra Danenberga, 1912–2011): 'Jewish ancestry, never tell anyone'. Which line it was said of isn't recorded. Peter's account (2026-10-27): 'Apocryphal from vecmama (Elvira); but who knows'.
There are Latvian Jewish Danenbergs, and some have contacted the family (Peter, 2026-10-27: 'they've hit us up'; the letters are in Peter's and his father's email, not yet archived).

evidence_against.note: Peter's FamilyTreeDNA myOrigins (v3, Family Finder): 0% Ashkenazi Jewish. An ethnicity estimate can miss a single distant ancestor, but shows no Jewish ancestry in roughly the last 5–6 generations on either side.
Peter's Y-DNA, his father's father's line, is N-Z16980 → A11470, a Baltic branch common in Latvia and rare among Ashkenazi Jews.

The Dannenberg surname of this line was registered in 1835 for a Latvian joiner's family on Gross-Bersen (Lielbērze) manor; the founder appears in 1826 as 'Jurre Tischler', without a surname. Courland's Jews also took mostly German-based surnames (Beider, Jewish Surnames in the Russian Empire), so the shared name isn't evidence either way.
Lutheran records throughout: baptisms, confirmations and church weddings (Elvīra's memoir; the parish books).

leads.decider: Peter's father's Family Finder test (ordered 2026-10-23): half his DNA comes from Arvīds, so it tests the Danenberg side directly. Also archive the letters from the Latvian Jewish Danenbergs.
leads.next_step: Wait for Dad's Family Finder results; collect the Jewish Danenbergs' letters (Peter's and his father's email).

CONFIRMED by the 1857 Priekuļi soul revision, read in full on 2026-10-27 (research/sweep/sirlaks-frontier, Round 3): its only Gibboi girl of Marija's age is Marri, 4, daughter of Marz Gibboi (50) and Anne (38) at Rauguļi, with her sister Christine, 2; the 1816 Mārcis is on the list too ('Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth', 41½, at the Ģiboļi farm) with a wife Anne of 38 and no Marija. In the tree since 2026-10-27: Raimonds's 1807 couple merged into I1020 × I1021 (the duplicates of the 2026-10-26 import, I1288 × I1291, retired); Kristīne (I1302) and Mārcis b. 1849 (I1300) their children (probable); the 1816 couple separate people (I1323 × I1324), Mārcis a son of Jānis × Masche (probable, 'Jahns Söhne'); Marija not linked to them; the Balodis line the family of the 1816 Mārcis's wife, no longer Peter's ancestry (possible links, kept). Marija's and Liene's links to Anna rest on the 1834 revision (probable); Dāvis's on his inference (possible); Pēteris Vīstucis as Anna's husband on his tree alone (possible).
evidence_for.quote: 1834.gada dvēseļu revīzijā dzīvo Vīstuču Pētera mājā, ir 27 gadus veca. divas meitas - Marija (8 gadi) un Liene (2 gadi).

evidence_for.quote: Viens no brāļiem Jānis Sirlaks 1869.gadā nopirka māju no Mārča Vīstuča. … Tātad pirms viņa tā tika dēvēta par Vīstuča māju. Turpināja saukt par “Vīstučiem”.
evidence_for.translation: One of the brothers, Jānis Sirlaks, bought the house in 1869 from Mārcis Vīstucis. … So before him it was called Vīstucis's house. It went on being called "Vīstuči".
